_about: Supporting data for the cuttle agent-experience research, 2026-08-18. Anonymized for public release: session labels S01..S46, services and products replaced with category descriptions, per-session summaries rewritten by a dedicated de-identification pass.

code_deltas.headline: The 2442c32..a91d105 window (2026-08-08 to 2026-08-17, 8 commits, 6 of them substantive) is entirely humanize/actionability maintenance plus a Chromium 150.0.7871.114.6 binary promotion - no new agent-facing verbs, no dialog/download/screenshot/viewer work at all. Three of the fixes are real behavioural bugs in the same layer cuttle's humanize.go lives in: isolated-world staleness after a click-driven navigation (a91d105), a ~7s/click wasted scroll budget when the page is pinned at a boundary (5494ac1), and frame-tree recursion that only walked one level deep (ec88026). The direction of the project is narrowing: CloakBrowser is doubling down on being a stealth *wrapper* around Playwright/Puppeteer (Python/JS/.NET parity on every fix) and is not building agent affordances - it has zero dialog handling, zero screenshot verb, zero download plumbing, and no SKILL.md/AGENTS.md/MCP surface. The most valuable extractions for cuttle are not the diffs themselves but three structural things their code reveals: the isolated-world hit-test that names the covering element, the headed-mode `viewportSize() === null` fallback, and their README's FingerprintJS table stating that screen-dimensions-vs-viewport mismatch is itself a "Virtual machine" detection - which reframes cuttle's viewer-sizing pain as a fingerprint problem with a known-correct fix.

items.what: cuttle's isolated world is created ONLY in the root frame (Page.getFrameTree -> frameTree.frame.id -> Page.createIsolatedWorld), so probeExpr/togglePollExpr run document.elementFromPoint in the main frame's document. elementFromPoint does not pierce iframes: for any click inside an iframe it returns the <iframe> element, whose box never moves and which carries no aria-expanded/pressed/checked. CloakBrowser just fixed the analogous blind spot by recursing the whole frame tree (ec88026, _iter_frames/iterFrames now walk depth-first instead of main+direct-children).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: internal/serve/humanize.go:1018 createWorld + probeExpr (~line 1064). Every click into a captcha widget, payment iframe, embedded SSO or consent frame silently gets NO settle gate (the iframe box is always stable) and NO post-click aria re-click (no toggle attr found -> verify degenerates). That is precisely the class of page where the gate was supposed to earn its keep. Fix: build one isolated world per frameId (map keyed sid+frameId), pick the frame by hit-testing the coordinate down the frame tree, and offset coords into frame space.

items.what: build_pointer_js hit-tests elementFromPoint(x,y) against the resolved target and, on a miss, returns {hit:false, covering: <tagName of whatever IS at that point>}, which ElementNotReceivingEventsError turns into the message "element is covered by <div>". A pointer miss is never silent and always names the blocker.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cloakbrowser/human/stealth_dom.py:build_pointer_js + actionability.py ElementNotReceivingEventsError. cuttle's probeExpr already resolves the element at (cx,cy) but returns only {x,y,w,h,tattr,tval} - it never reports WHAT is there. Adding tag/id/class/role to the probe and logging it when awaitStable exhausts its budget or when the toggle verify re-clicks would give agents the single missing sentence for pain point 4: 'your click at (x,y) is landing on <div class=cdk-overlay-backdrop>, not your button'. This is the cheapest available fix for the invisible-overlay problem and needs no new verb.

items.what: CloakBrowser humanizes Locator.scroll_into_view_if_needed / el.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded, replacing Playwright's instant CDP scroll with a paced wheel burst (accelerate/cruise/decelerate + overshoot) before every click.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's humanizer only intercepts Input.dispatchMouseEvent / Input.dispatchKeyEvent / Input.insertText (internal/serve/humanize.go:136-138 and the `bytes.Contains(data, []byte("Input."))` fast-path at :388). Playwright's actionability scroll goes out as DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded, which cuttle passes through untouched - so almost every humanized click in cuttle is preceded by an instant, event-less scroll jump with zero wheel events. A page that watches for wheel events before a click sees a teleport. Intercept DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded, read the box, and satisfy it with the existing planScroll wheel burst.

items.what: Humanized scroll-into-view now reads {y: window.scrollY, maxY: scrollHeight - clientHeight} and bails immediately when the element is fully visible but off-centre AND the page is already pinned at the boundary in the needed direction. Previously the scroll loop burned its full budget (~7s per click) emitting wheel events that could never move the page.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Directly applicable if cuttle takes the DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded interception above; the same 'is this loop capable of changing anything?' guard also applies to cuttle's awaitStable settle gate (internal/serve/humanize.go:782), which currently polls its whole budget on an element that cannot become stable. Their measured cost was 7s/click of pure waste - cuttle's click is already ~0.5s and the settle budget is the part users feel.

items.what: The isolated world used for pre-action DOM reads was only invalidated on goto, so a navigation driven by a click or a form submit left it bound to the dead document and every subsequent humanized action failed with element-not-attached. Fixed by wiring page.on('framenavigated') -> stealth.invalidate() for the main frame, in Python sync+async, JS Playwright, JS Puppeteer and .NET. Regression introduced in 0.5.6.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already handles this better and reactively: internal/serve/humanize.go:945 evaluate() detects the protocol error on a stale contextId, drops h.worlds[sid], and query() rebuilds and retries exactly once (comment at :936 calls out navigate-then-click by name). No change needed - but their regression is the argument for keeping cuttle's humanize_click_test.go covering click-driven navigation followed by an immediate second click, since this is the exact bug an event-driven design walked into twice.

items.what: humanScrollIntoView explicitly handles page.viewportSize() returning null: headed launches default to no_viewport so the page tracks the real OS window, and the code falls back to window.innerWidth/innerHeight read through the isolated world (VIEWPORT_JS), throwing a named 'Viewport size not available' error only if both fail.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle runs headed Chrome on Xvfb, so every driver attached over CDP sees viewportSize()===null and any driver logic keyed on it silently degrades. Two actions: (a) if cuttle ever computes geometry server-side, use window.innerWidth/innerHeight in the isolated world, not a declared viewport; (b) internal/cli/SKILL.md should tell agents that cuttle sessions are no_viewport and that page.viewport_size is null by design - that is a five-line doc fix for a confusing failure mode.

items.what: README's FingerprintJS troubleshooting table lists 'Virtual machine' detection with cause 'Screen dimensions don't match viewport' and fix '--fingerprint-screen-width/height matching viewport'. Their whole recommended anti-bot config is proxy + geoip + headless=False + humanize.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This reframes cuttle pain point 1. internal/fingerprint/args.go:354-357 sets --fingerprint-screen-width from the seed table and --window-size = width x (height - taskbar); the window not filling the 1920x1080 VNC framebuffer is the CORRECT stealth behaviour, and enlarging the window to fill the viewer would create exactly the mismatch FPJS flags as a VM. The right fix is the other direction: size the Xvfb/KasmVNC framebuffer per seed to the seed's spoofed screen, or have agents pin the seed's screen to the framebuffer. cuttle already supports the latter today - parseConnectionParams (internal/serve/http.go:194-197) forwards any unknown query key as --fingerprint-<key>, so connecting with ?fingerprint=X&screen-width=1920&screen-height=1080 yields a 1920x1032 window on the 1920x1080 framebuffer. That is undocumented in SKILL.md and is the single highest-value doc addition available.

items.what: the deployed daemon exposes POST /fingerprint/{seed}/close: tears down that seed's Chrome immediately, frees the slot, keeps the persistent profile, idempotent (returns {seed, terminated:false} with 200 if not running). Shipped in 0.5.2.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's route table (internal/serve/http.go:53-65) has GET /, /json/version, /json/list, GET|PUT /profile/{seed}/state, GET /downloads[/{name}], and the two WS routes - there is no per-seed teardown. An agent that wants a clean slate for one seed must either wait out the idle timeout or take the whole daemon down. cuttle's chromePool.status() (internal/serve/pool.go:724) already mirrors the deployed daemon's status payload field-for-field including idle_cleanup_pending, so this is the one remaining gap in that API's parity. Pair it with a `cuttle context rm <name>` / `cuttle restart <seed>` CLI verb.
items.ref: bin/the deployed daemon handle_close (routes at bin/the deployed daemon:891)

items.what: `cloakbrowser info` is a real doctor command: reports which binary will actually launch, runs a live launch probe, flags missing system libraries on Linux, checks fonts and GeoIP and optional deps, prints license tier, supports --quick (skip launch test) and --json (machine-readable). `info --proxy <url>` additionally resolves the exit IP, timezone and locale a launch WOULD apply through that proxy, without launching.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's `status` reports the running daemon; there is no preflight. An agent given a proxy has no way to confirm the geoip resolution before burning a session, and no machine-readable environment check. `cuttle doctor --json` (fonts present, stealth binary version, backend reachable, driver CLIs installed) plus `cuttle status --proxy <url>` resolving tz/locale/exit-IP would collapse a whole category of 'why is this session UTC/en-US' confusion. The --json flag matters most: agents parse, they don't read tables.

items.what: Humanize behaviour is a named-preset + fully-overridable config surface: presets `default` and `careful`, ~35 tunables in HumanConfig (typing_delay 70 / typing_delay_spread 40 / typing_pause_chance 0.1, mistype_chance 0.02, field_switch_delay 800-1500ms, mouse_overshoot_chance 0.15, scroll_target_zone, idle_between_actions + idle_between_duration, initial_cursor_x/y), passed as human_preset= / human_config= at launch. Plus `page._original` as a documented escape hatch to the un-patched Playwright page for calls that need raw speed.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: internal/serve/humanize.go:36-112 hard-codes every constant (fittsA, prePressMs, clickHoldMs, scrollDtMs, the 80-rune insertText cap). cuttle's own docs concede ~0.5s/click and ~130ms/char - nearly 2x their 70ms default - with no way to dial it down for a trusted target or off for a bulk step. Two concrete asks: (a) a per-connection query param (?humanize=off|fast|careful) since parseConnectionParams already passes arbitrary keys through, giving agents the `_original` escape hatch at the mux layer; (b) field_switch_delay and idle_between_actions are two behaviours cuttle's humanizer does not model at all - the pause between finishing one field and clicking the next is one of the most obvious bot tells in a login form, which is exactly cuttle pain point 2.

items.what: Typed actionability error hierarchy: ElementNotAttachedError / NotVisible / NotStable / NotEnabled / NotEditable / NotReceivingEvents, each carrying the selector and the failed check name, formatted as "Element 'X' failed <check> check: <reason>". Per-action check sets (CHECKS_CLICK, CHECKS_HOVER, CHECKS_INPUT, CHECKS_FOCUS, CHECKS_CHECK) and a Playwright-matched backoff ladder [100,250,500,1000]ms.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's settle gate is deliberately fail-open (internal/serve/humanize.go:782 awaitStable 'presses anyway' when out of budget) and the mux surfaces nothing to the driver when it does. Fail-open is right for a transparent CDP proxy, but the information should not evaporate: emit a structured line to `cuttle logs` (or a Runtime console message the driver can see) naming the check that gave up, the coordinate, and the covering element. Right now an agent whose click was swallowed and re-clicked has no way to know either happened.

items.what: Their isolated-world DOM reads reimplement a deliberately narrow subset of Playwright's selector grammar (css, :has-text(".."), text=, xpath=, trailing >> nth=N) and return 'unsupported' for anything richer (>> chaining, internal:* engines from get_by_*, :visible, :nth-match, layout pseudos), falling back to the real Playwright read rather than guessing. Stated rule: 'correctness wins on tie - a mis-resolved element yields wrong coordinates'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Not applicable as code (cuttle operates on coordinates, never selectors, which is a structurally better position). Worth recording as the reason cuttle should NOT grow a selector layer in the mux: this file is 219 lines of grammar reimplementation that still bails on get_by_role, the API agents actually use. cuttle's coordinate-level interception is the cheaper correct answer.

items.what: page.selectOption re-dispatches to the main frame's selectOption, which the frame patcher routes back to page.selectOption; binding the saved original to the page looped forever. Fixed by binding to page.mainFrame().selectOption. Regression test uses a depth counter that throws rather than hanging.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Pure wrapper-monkeypatching hazard - cuttle has no equivalent because it intercepts at the CDP frame level. Included only to close the loop on the commit list; the transferable part is the test technique (a depth guard that converts an infinite loop into a failing assertion), which suits cuttle's humanize re-click path where a swallowed-click re-click could in principle re-trigger itself.

items.what: Negative finding, verified by grep across the whole repo: CloakBrowser has NO dialog/alert/beforeunload handling, NO screenshot affordance, NO download plumbing, NO upload/file-chooser support, NO page-state digest, NO element-reference scheme, and no SKILL.md / AGENTS.md / MCP tool definitions of any kind. The only occurrence of the word 'dialog' in README.md is about the macOS Gatekeeper prompt. Their entire agent-facing surface is 6 CLI verbs (login, logout, install, info, update, clear-cache) plus 5 the deployed daemon HTTP routes.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle is already ahead of its closest competitor on every one of the four named pain points except humanized scroll: `cuttle downloads`, GET /downloads[/{name}], profile state snapshot/restore, and the keep-alive tab have no counterpart here. Do not expect this repo to solve dialogs/screenshots for you - it is a stealth wrapper, not an agent runtime. Mine it for humanize internals only, and look elsewhere (or build) for the dialog/overlay affordance.
items.ref: rg over README.md + cloakbrowser/ + js/ + bin/ for dialog|screenshot|accept_download|beforeunload

items.what: --fingerprint-taskbar-height flag with per-platform binary defaults (Windows 48, macOS 95, Linux 0), used so screen.availHeight stays coherent with the spoofed platform in headed mode. The 150.0.7871.114.6 binary notes also call out 'improved headed window geometry' for the Windows persona as a distinct coherence workstream.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: internal/fingerprint/args.go:357 already subtracts a taskbar from the window height, so the concept is present - but the value is not exposed as a knob and its coherence with screen.availHeight/availWidth under the Windows (amd64) vs macOS (arm64) personas is worth a golden-test assertion. Their treating headed geometry as a recurring binary-level coherence problem is a signal that this is a real detection vector, not cosmetics.
items.ref: README.md:735 flags table; CHANGELOG 150.0.7871.114.6 'Windows fidelity' bullet

items.what: Release-engineering surface: a standing `preview` release channel (release_channel="preview" / CLOAKBROWSER_RELEASE_CHANNEL, resolves to Stable on platforms with no Preview build), CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION for exact rollback pinning, and CLI diagnostics that print requested-vs-resolved channel plus the exact version that will launch. Currently Stable 150.0.7871.114.6 / Preview 151.0.7922.108.2.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle pins the engine in packages/browser/versions.env with no runtime channel or rollback path - an agent hitting a stealth regression has no 'drop back one build' escape. Not urgent while cuttle ships one self-built engine, but their pattern (channel is a standing setting, not a pin; diagnostics always print requested vs resolved) is the right shape if cuttle ever ships more than one pinned Chromium.

code_deltas.headline: Only 7 commits landed in ~3 months, but two of them are structural: b0b9db9 added a runtime-policy layer (backend/runtime.py) that splits the product into "native-window" (Windows/macOS, browser in a real desktop window) and "vnc" (Linux Docker/KasmVNC) viewer modes, surfacing `host_os`/`runtime_mode`/`viewer_mode` in every API response so clients know which affordances exist; c55fbb1 rebuilt the profile schema and deliberately DELETED the editable persona knobs (user_agent, platform, gpu_vendor/renderer, hardware_concurrency, headless), replacing them with runtime-derived persona plus a 3-value gpu_family enum - the same "persona is not user-editable" stance cuttle already takes. The direction is: fewer knobs, more runtime self-description, and hardening the seams (auth split /api/health vs /api/status in 15dccb2, startup-time license/binary pre-resolution off the launch path in 214f068). For cuttle the two highest-value transfers are not in the delta at all but in the code the delta touches: a per-profile Xvnc framebuffer sized to that profile's spoofed screen with the browser viewport pinned to it (this is exactly cuttle pain #1, and cuttle's fixed shared `Xvnc :99 -geometry 1920x1080` is the cause), and an HTTP clipboard relay (POST/GET /api/profiles/{id}/clipboard) that lets a programmatic caller stage text into the session's X clipboard and paste it instead of typing (cuttle pain #2 - cuttle's clipboard path exists only inside the human viewer's JS, not in the daemon API). Notably neither project has any screenshot verb, download endpoint, dialog/alert visibility, or upload/file-chooser support - cuttle is actually ahead on downloads, and nobody in this niche has solved invisible native dialogs.

items.what: Each profile gets its OWN Xvnc, started with `-geometry {screen_width}x{screen_height}` taken from that profile's spoofed screen (browser_manager.launch -> vnc.start_vnc(width=profile['screen_width'], height=profile['screen_height'])); displays allocated from 100 upward, ws ports 6100+n.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the direct fix for pain #1. cuttle's ops/docker/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh starts ONE `Xvnc :99 -geometry 1920x1080` shared by every seed, while internal/fingerprint/args.go sizes --window-size to the seed's spoofed screen - so a 1366x768 seed can only ever occupy 50% of the framebuffer. Per-seed X server (or per-seed RandR mode set on :99) makes the window fill the viewer by construction instead of by luck.

items.what: Browser viewport is pinned to the framebuffer minus browser chrome: `launch_options['viewport'] = {width: screen_width, height: screen_height - 133}`, set only when a display was allocated (VNC mode). Test asserts the exact value {1920, 947}.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The 133px constant is the empirical Chrome-chrome height on their headed Linux stack; combining framebuffer-geometry with a viewport pinned to (framebuffer - chrome) is what makes the page fill the viewer. cuttle sets --window-size in internal/fingerprint/args.go but never reconciles it with the VNC framebuffer.

items.what: noVNC client configured `rfb.scaleViewport = true; rfb.resizeSession = false; rfb.showDotCursor = true` so any framebuffer size scales to fit the panel without renegotiating the session.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's ops/docker/bin/vnc-viewer.html is a hand-rolled minimal viewer; scaleViewport is the cheap half of the pain-#1 fix (page is legible even when framebuffer != panel), and resizeSession=false is the correct choice for a fingerprinted session where a client-driven resize would change the spoofed screen.

items.what: POST /api/profiles/{id}/clipboard writes text into the profile's X CLIPBOARD by spawning `xclip -selection clipboard` with DISPLAY=:{display} on stdin; the xclip process is kept ALIVE (it must be, to serve paste requests) and tracked per-display so the previous one is killed before a new one spawns.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Directly attacks pain #2. cuttle has no server-side clipboard at all - internal/serve/humanize.go rewrites Input.insertText into real keystrokes at ~130ms/char, so a 40-char password is ~5s of typo-injected typing. A `cuttle clipboard set <seed> <text>` + a CDP-side Ctrl+V is O(1) and never mistypes a secret. The kept-alive-xclip and kill-the-previous-one detail is the non-obvious part.

items.what: GET /api/profiles/{id}/clipboard reads the clipboard by evaluating `window.__clipboardText` over CDP across ALL pages in the context, falling back to `xclip -o` (5s timeout, empty string on failure) - because Chrome under KasmVNC does not own the X11 CLIPBOARD selection, so xclip alone reads nothing.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The discovery is the finding: X-level clipboard reads do not work for a headed Chrome under KasmVNC. Any cuttle 'read what the human copied in the viewer' feature must go through CDP/page-eval, not xclip. Same constraint applies to cuttle's ops/docker stack.

items.what: An init script installed via context.add_init_script AND re-evaluated on already-open pages captures copy events and Ctrl/Cmd+C selections into `window.__clipboardText`, because Chrome's VNC-driven copy fires no DOM event reachable any other way.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Shows the 'inject once for new pages, plus back-fill existing pages' pattern cuttle would need for any per-seed page instrumentation over CDP (Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument + a loop over existing targets). cuttle already does per-page work in internal/serve/pool.go (focus-emulation pin, locale override) so the hook point exists.

items.what: HEAD commit gates that clipboard init script behind `if self.runtime.viewer_mode == 'vnc'` so native-window profiles never get `window.__clipboardText` injected into every page; test asserts add_init_script is NOT awaited in native mode.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: An injected page global is a detection tell and a permanent fingerprint surface. cuttle's stealth posture (golden.json tripwire, clark patch series) makes 'never inject a global unless a consumer exists in this mode' the right default for any future page instrumentation.

items.what: Viewer intercepts Ctrl+V on the container at capture phase (before noVNC's canvas listener), stopPropagation + preventDefault, POSTs the host clipboard to the server, then sends an EXPLICIT full Ctrl-down/V-down/V-up/Ctrl-up keysym sequence - because the user may have released Ctrl during the async round-trip.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's ops/docker/bin/vnc-viewer.html sends the clipboard on the same socket as the keystrokes and relies on TCP ordering to be race-free (its own comment says so). CloakBrowser hit the exact race when the clipboard write is an out-of-band HTTP call. If cuttle ever adds an API-side clipboard set, it inherits this race and needs the same synthesized modifier sequence.

items.what: Viewer polls GET .../clipboard every 2s to mirror the session clipboard back to the host, and self-cancels the poll loop permanently on the first error.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Polling is the only VNC->host direction that works for Chrome copies (see the xclip finding). The self-cancelling loop is a decent pattern but also a footgun - one transient 502 kills clipboard sync for the rest of the session with only a console.warn. cuttle should surface such degradations, not silently disable them.

items.what: Per-profile `humanize` boolean (default FALSE) plus `human_preset` enum ('default' | 'careful') persisted in the DB and passed into the launch call per profile.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's humanization is a daemon-wide `--humanize` flag (internal/serve/serve.go:149, internal/serve/wsproxy.go:177) applied to every seed and every connection, costing ~0.5s/click and ~130ms/char unconditionally. A per-seed (or per-CDP-connection) level - off / fast / careful - would let an agent burn realism only where the target actually profiles behavior. This is the single biggest agent-throughput lever in internal/serve/humanize.go.

items.what: Conflicting user launch args are rejected with a named, actionable error before launch: any `--remote-debugging-port`/`--remote-debugging-address` in profile.launch_args raises ValueError('Manager owns remote debugging configuration; remove: <the exact args>'), which the API maps to HTTP 400 (not 500).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle accepts extra Chrome args in the fingerprint arg-builder (internal/fingerprint/args.go) and a caller passing --remote-debugging-port would silently break the multiplexer. Naming the offending tokens in the error is the cheap agent-ergonomics win; the ValueError-to-400 vs Exception-to-500 split is the other half (agents retry 500s, they fix 400s).

items.what: All request models gained `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')`, so an unknown field is a 422 naming the field instead of being silently dropped.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: An agent that misremembers a knob name currently gets silent no-op behavior in most tools. Strict rejection turns a subtle 'my setting did nothing' debugging session into one error line. Applies to cuttle's CLI flag parsing and any JSON config path (internal/config).

items.what: CDP readiness is VERIFIED, not assumed: _wait_for_cdp polls http://127.0.0.1:{port}/json/version for 10s and additionally asserts the returned webSocketDebuggerUrl actually contains ':{port}/' - catching a browser that attached to a different port. Wrapped in a 3-attempt loop that reserves a FRESH OS-assigned port each try and closes/releases everything on failure.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's pool has launch backoff (internal/serve/pool.go) but the port-identity assertion is a distinct check: a Chrome that grabbed a different debugging port produces a live-but-wrong CDP endpoint, which surfaces to the agent as inexplicable cross-seed behavior. Cheap to add to cuttle's readiness poll.

items.what: CDP ports are reserved by binding 127.0.0.1:0, reading the OS-assigned port, closing, and tracking it in an in-process set (20 retries for uniqueness), with explicit release on stop, crash, and every failure path.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Mostly convergent with cuttle's pool, but the release-on-every-path discipline (including the `context.on('close')` crash handler calling _dispose_running) is worth diffing against internal/serve/pool.go's teardown paths.

items.what: CDP is fronted on the manager's single HTTP port with FOUR path aliases for the target list (/cdp/json, /cdp/json/, /cdp/json/list, /cdp/json/list/) plus /cdp/json/version(/), rewriting every webSocketDebuggerUrl to point back through the proxy, and a separate page-level WS route /cdp/devtools/{path:path}.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's internal/serve/wsproxy.go + http.go do the same job. The alias set is the lesson: different drivers (playwright-core, puppeteer, chrome-remote-interface) hit different spellings, and a missing trailing-slash variant looks to the agent like 'CDP is broken'. Worth auditing cuttle's http.go route table against all four.

items.what: GET /api/profiles/{id}/cdp (plain HTTP) returns {cdp_url, usage: "playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp('http://<host>/api/profiles/<id>/cdp')"} - a self-describing endpoint that exists partly so the SPA catch-all doesn't serve index.html on that path.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle prints attach commands in internal/cli/briefing.go, but only at `cuttle up` time. An agent that lost the briefing (compaction, new session) has no way to re-derive the attach recipe from the daemon itself. A GET on the CDP URL returning the exact driver invocation makes the endpoint self-documenting.

items.what: Every profile/launch/status response carries `runtime_mode` and `viewer_mode` (native|docker, native-window|vnc), and the frontend branches on them - hiding the clipboard-sync checkbox entirely when viewer_mode != 'vnc' (9dd49cf), rendering a NativeWindowStatus panel instead of a VNC canvas.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's `status`/`up` output should carry a machine-readable capability descriptor (viewer available? downloads dir? humanize level? context creation allowed?) so an agent stops guessing which verbs are live. Today an agent learns `--allow-context-creation` is off only by getting a blocked Target.createBrowserContext.

items.what: Unavailable affordances fail with typed, reason-carrying errors rather than generic ones: HTTP 409 'Clipboard relay is available only in Docker/VNC mode', WS close 4005 'VNC unavailable in native-window mode', WS close 4004 'Profile not running', VNCManager.validate_available() failing at STARTUP ('Linux Manager requires the Docker image with KasmVNC installed') instead of at first launch.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Fail-at-startup-with-the-reason is the pattern cuttle should apply to its own preconditions (fonts, Xvnc, geoip DB, profile dir writability). Distinct WS close codes per cause are also directly usable in internal/serve/wsproxy.go where drivers currently just see a dropped socket.

items.what: /api/status is now auth-gated and a new unauthenticated, detail-free /api/health was added purely as the liveness probe (contributed PR #48); the follow-up commit repointed the native launcher's readiness poll from /api/status to /api/health after it broke.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Two-commit sequence showing the trap: the moment status carries anything sensitive, every readiness poll built on it breaks. cuttle's CLI waits on the daemon before printing the briefing - that wait should target a probe endpoint that will never grow auth or detail.

items.what: WebSocket CSWSH protection that deliberately allows non-browser clients: if an Origin header is present it must match Host, but a MISSING Origin is allowed - because Playwright/Puppeteer/curl never send one.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle exposes CDP on 127.0.0.1:9222 with no origin check; any page the user browses can WebSocket into it and drive the farm (the classic localhost-CDP attack). This is the exact rule that blocks it without breaking driver attach. Applies to internal/serve/wsproxy.go and http.go.

items.what: On first launch, seeds the profile with a Bookmarks bar (folders: Detection Tests, Fingerprint, Headers & TLS, reCAPTCHA - ~22 bookmarks incl. CreepJS, Pixelscan, BrowserScan, Turnstile, TLS fingerprint) and a Preferences file setting DuckDuckGo as default search - only when those files are absent.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Two things at once: (a) a browser profile with zero bookmarks and a stock search engine is itself weak evidence of automation, (b) it hands the human at the VNC viewer a one-click stealth-verification suite. cuttle has docs/STEALTH-VERIFICATION.md and packages/browser/validate/ but nothing in-profile; seeding this at profile creation in the profile store costs nothing.

items.what: /api/status reports Windows-persona font health (`windows_fonts_present`/`_required`/`_complete`) by calling into the browser lib's _WINDOWS_FONT_TELLS + _count_fonts_present, gated to the docker+linux case where that persona is emulated; the UI shows an amber 'Fonts incomplete' warning badge.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle ships ops/docker/winfonts (metric-compatible free packs) and ops/docker/macfonts/metrics.json but has no runtime assertion that the packs actually resolved in the running container - a silently missing font pack is a stealth regression that the golden.json tripwire cannot catch because it lives outside the arg-builder. A font-tell count in `cuttle status` is a cheap self-diagnosis.

items.what: Schema rebuild DELETED the editable persona fields user_agent, platform, gpu_vendor, gpu_renderer, hardware_concurrency, headless; the code comment is explicit: 'Persona is always determined by the runtime, not editable profile data' (macos persona on macOS host, windows otherwise), with GPU reduced to a 3-value enum and Windows-only overrides skipped on macOS as 'incoherent'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Independent confirmation of cuttle's non-negotiable (Apple-Silicon persona pinned on arm64, Windows on amd64, internal/fingerprint/args.go). A direct competitor tried per-profile free-text persona fields, shipped them, and then ripped them out. Reinforces resisting any future request for a --user-agent or --platform flag.

items.what: Per-profile `color_scheme` (light | dark | no-preference) passed to launch as a real Chromium-level emulation setting, persisted with the identity.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: prefers-color-scheme is a stable, queryable fingerprint bit that should be part of a seed's identity, not left at the container default for every seed. cuttle's internal/fingerprint has the per-seed screen table and locale/timezone but no color-scheme derivation - every cuttle seed presumably reports the same value, which is a cross-seed correlation tell.

items.what: Per-profile `extension_paths` (unpacked extension directories) and `allow_3p_cookies` (mapped to --fingerprint-allow-3p-cookies) as first-class 'compatibility controls', separate from the free-text launch_args escape hatch.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has no extension-loading path. Agents periodically need one (cookie-banner blocker, a solver, an internal test extension), and today the only route is hand-crafted Chrome args that would collide with cuttle's arg-builder. Worth deciding explicitly rather than by omission - though it conflicts with cuttle's KISS rule until a concrete caller exists.

items.what: Per-profile `auto_launch` flag; on daemon startup auto_launch_all() launches each flagged profile with asyncio.wait_for(timeout=60), logging and skipping failures rather than aborting startup.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle spawns a Chrome per seed on first demand, so an agent's first attach eats the cold-start. A declarative 'warm these seeds at daemon start' (a flag in the profile store, honored by internal/serve/pool.go) removes that latency and makes `cuttle up` mean the farm is actually ready.

items.what: Anything slow was moved out of the launch path into startup: resolve_binary_status() runs in a thread during lifespan to resolve license tier, version, and PRE-DOWNLOAD the multi-hundred-MB binary, explicitly so the download 'never blocks a launch or auto-launch's 60s timeout'; it never raises (keyless binary stays usable on any failure).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle bakes Chromium into the image so the download case doesn't apply, but the principle maps to geoip DB load, profile auth-state restore, and font cache warm - anything that can turn a first launch into a timeout. The never-raise-with-degraded-fallback shape is also the right one for cuttle's geoip.

items.what: Proxy normalization accepts host:port:user:pass and host:port (not just full URLs) and validates the normalized result with a specific message per failure ('Invalid proxy scheme X. Must be http, https, or socks5.', 'Proxy URL missing hostname/port: <url>').
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: host:port:user:pass is the format every proxy vendor's dashboard emits and the one agents paste. cuttle's internal/fingerprint/proxy.go handles schemeless URLs (EnsureProxyScheme) and socks normalization but not the 4-colon vendor form; and its errors should name which component is missing.

items.what: An RFB client-message filter/rewriter sits in the VNC proxy: it parses noVNC's batched multi-message frames, WHITELISTS safe encodings in SetEncodings (comment: blocklisting was tried and 'we had wrong numbers'), rewrites the 6-byte standard PointerEvent into KasmVNC's 11-byte form, skips known extension types (150, 248, 252, 255) by size rather than bailing, and refuses to forward a partial message because that desyncs the stream. KasmVNC 1.3.3 crashes on unsupported types.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's ops/docker/bin/vnc-viewer.html speaks to KasmVNC directly, so it dodges this today - but these are the exact landmines if cuttle ever proxies RFB (for auth, multi-viewer, or per-seed routing) or bumps noVNC. The whitelist-not-blocklist conclusion and the never-forward-partial-frames rule are hard-won.

items.what: KasmVNC's BinaryClipboard (type 180) server messages are parsed and translated into standard RFB ServerCutText (type 3) so stock noVNC fires its normal `clipboard` event; ServerCutText is Latin-1 per spec, so CJK/emoji degrade to '?'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's vnc-viewer.html already parses type 180 natively (readBinaryClipboard) - convergent, and cuttle's approach is better because it avoids the Latin-1 lossy hop entirely. Worth knowing cuttle is ahead here and should not 'standardize' onto ServerCutText.

items.what: Launch adds --use-angle=swiftshader only in VNC mode (no GPU on the X server) and --test-type always, with a comment tying --test-type to the Linux Docker no-sandbox warning path and noting Playwright already supplies --disable-infobars.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Worth diffing against cuttle's internal/fingerprint/args.go: mode-conditional GPU args and the reason each compatibility arg exists. Any arg change in cuttle trips the golden.json tripwire, so this is a review-and-decide item, not a copy.

items.what: Delete ordering is explicit and commented: stop the browser, then delete the DB row, THEN rmtree the user_data_dir - 'DB first - if this fails, filesystem is untouched'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Maps to `cuttle purge-profile` in internal/cli/commands.go and the profile store. Getting the order backwards leaves an orphan record pointing at a deleted dir, which then fails every subsequent launch with a confusing error.

items.what: A dependency-free .env loader (backend/env_file.py) reads KEY=VALUE from the repo-root .env into os.environ WITHOUT overriding values already present, so Docker -e and real shell exports always win over the file.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's config already maps flags to CUTTLE_* env vars (internal/serve/serve.go). The precedence rule (real env beats file, file beats default) is the one users expect and the one that avoids 'why is my -e ignored' support traffic if cuttle ever grows a config file.

items.what: Auth is raw ASGI middleware rather than Starlette's BaseHTTPMiddleware, with an explicit comment that the latter 'breaks WebSocket routes (wraps request body, preventing WS upgrade)'; unauthenticated WS gets close code 4401 after the mandatory receive() of websocket.connect, HTTP gets 401 JSON; token compare uses hmac.compare_digest for both header and cookie.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Framework-specific, but the shape matters if cuttle ever puts auth in front of :9222/:6080: an auth layer that silently breaks the CDP WS upgrade is the worst possible failure mode for an agent, and a distinct close code (4401) is what makes it diagnosable.

items.what: Container entrypoint is defensive about crash residue: pkill of stale `Xvnc :N`, cloakbrowser/chromium processes and xclip, delete of SingletonLock/SingletonCookie/SingletonSocket under /data/profiles, and rm of /tmp/.X1*-lock - plus a per-launch singleton-lock unlink that is explicitly SKIPPED in native mode ('Native mode must let Chromium arbitrate profile ownership itself').
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already clears Singleton* (internal/serve/pool.go:588-603, ops/helm deployment.yaml) so the core is covered - but the stale X11 lock (/tmp/.X*-lock) and orphan-Xvnc sweep are extra cases cuttle's ops/docker/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh may not handle on an unclean container restart with a reused volume.

items.what: Full command/tool surface at HEAD is 17 HTTP routes and 2 WS routes: auth status/login/logout; profiles list/create/get/update/delete; launch; stop; per-profile status; /api/health; /api/status; clipboard set/get; cdp info + json/version + json/list (with aliases); WS /vnc and WS /cdp (+ /cdp/devtools/{path}). There is NO screenshot, NO download, NO upload/file-chooser, NO dialog/alert handling, NO tab list, NO page-state digest, NO element-reference scheme, NO wait primitive, and no MCP server or agent skill file (AGENTS.md is about their `bd` issue tracker, not the browser).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The comparison cuts both ways. cuttle already beats them on downloads (`cuttle downloads [name [dest]]`, GET /downloads served from the seed profile dir - internal/serve/downloads.go), on tab/session control (keep-alive tab, blocked context creation, per-seed auth-state snapshot/restore in internal/serve/state.go), and on an agent-facing skill (internal/cli/SKILL.md). Their only affordances cuttle lacks are the clipboard relay and per-profile viewer sizing. Crucially, pain #3 (screenshots) and pain #4 (invisible native dialogs/alerts/overlays) are unaddressed by BOTH projects - there is no prior art to copy here, so anything cuttle builds (a `cuttle screenshot` verb, a Page.javascriptDialogOpening watcher surfaced in `cuttle status`, a dialog-state field in the briefing) is net-new differentiation rather than catch-up.

code_deltas.headline: Nothing new shipped as a binary since cuttle's fork point: the latest GitHub release is still chromium-v148.0.7778.96-stealth5 (2026-06-01), and the local clone is a shallow graft at df1afb6 (2026-06-22) with no branches or tags beyond it. The entire post-stealth5 delta is 10 unreleased files on main: two new patches (0027-analyser-node-noise, 0047-suppress-cdc-globals), a Python-launcher pass that pins seed-derived screen size + derives the Playwright viewport from it and auto-enables proxy-coherent WebRTC, plus a local JA3/JA4 ClientHello capture harness and its unit tests. The project's direction is entirely engine-side stealth plus validation harnesses; it deliberately owns none of the agent-interaction surface (its only CLI verbs are info/fetch/clear, and its agent story is "use vercel agent-browser over CDP"), so it offers nothing on cuttle's dialogs/overlays, downloads, screenshots, or secret-typing pain. Of the two new patches, 0027 is a genuine gap-closer worth cherry-picking with a correction, and 0047 is dead code in cuttle's headed container and would introduce a louder tell than it hides.

items.what: There is no newer stealth tag or release than the one cuttle forked at. Remote tags via `gh api repos/.../tags` and `gh release list` both stop at chromium-v148.0.7778.96-stealth5 (published 2026-06-01); v0.2.0/v0.2.1 are PyPI package tags for the Python launcher only, not new binaries. The local clone is grafted (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` = true), so `log df1afb6..HEAD` is empty by construction - the real delta is `git diff chromium-v148.0.7778.96-stealth5 HEAD`, 10 files.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: packages/browser/versions.env's pin at stealth5 is current. There is no engine rebase to chase; only two unreleased patch files to evaluate. Any future check should diff tags, not the shallow log.

items.what: New patch on third_party/blink/renderer/modules/webaudio/realtime_analyser.cc adding seed-derived noise to AnalyserNode.getFloatFrequencyData (multiplicative scale ~3e-11 plus a ~1e-7 additive offset, keyed clark::seed::Hash("audio.analyser")) and getByteFrequencyData (per-bin +/-1 LSB from clark_h ^ i*0x9E3779B97F4A7C15). Closes the case where a detector reads the frequency domain via AnalyserNode instead of the AudioContext destination buffer, which patch 0026 does not cover. Include paths are third_party/blink/common/clark_{seed,fingerprint_switches}.h - exactly what cuttle's build-linux.sh stages (packages/browser/build/build-linux.sh:272-277), and the same paths cuttle's existing 0026 patch already uses.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's series (packages/browser/patches/, 24 patches) has 0026-audio-fingerprint-noise but no 0027, so AnalyserNode frequency data is still bit-identical to stock across every seed - a per-seed audio fingerprint that silently collapses to one value for any site reading the analyser. Drop-in cherry-pick into packages/browser/patches/, no build-driver change needed; renderer-side so it fires in cuttle's headed container.

items.what: Defect in 0027 as written: the float path applies scale+offset to db_mag, but the byte path adds a raw +/-1 to the *unmodified* scaled_value. The two APIs are specified to be derivable from each other (byte = 255*(db - minDecibels)*range_scale), so a detector that reads both and cross-checks finds a systematic disagreement that stock Chrome never shows. Worse, the byte perturbation is content-independent: the same fixed +/-1 pattern per bin index on every buffer, so a detector sampling silence sees a stable synthetic mask.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Cherry-picking verbatim would trade a missing-noise tell for a coherence tell - the exact class of bug clark's own 0.2.0 notes are full of (dead patch sites, incoherent getters). Before landing in packages/browser/patches/, derive the byte value from the already-noised float (apply clark_scale/clark_offset once to db_mag, then convert), and regenerate internal/fingerprint/testdata/golden.json only if arg output changes (it will not - this is binary-side).

items.what: New V8 extension registered in headless/lib/renderer/headless_content_renderer_client.cc that pre-defines cdc_/__webdriver*/__selenium*/__fxdriver*/__lastWatir* as non-configurable undefined, then replaces Object.defineProperty with a JS wrapper that silently returns the target object for any property name starting with cdc_, __webdriver, __selenium, or __$webdriver.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Do not take it, for four independent reasons. (1) It lives in headless_content_renderer_client.cc, which is only linked into the headless shell - cuttle's image runs headed (internal/serve/serve.go:245 appends --headless=false), so it is dead code there. (2) The Object.defineProperty replacement is a plain JS function: Function.prototype.toString.call(Object.defineProperty) leaks its source instead of '[native code]' and .name becomes '', which CreepJS-class native-function checks read directly - a far louder signal than the globals it hides. (3) cdc_ globals are ChromeDriver/Selenium artifacts; cuttle attaches raw CDP via internal/serve/wsproxy.go and never has them. (4) Swallowing a legitimate defineProperty (returning o rather than defining or throwing) will break real sites whose bundlers namespace on those prefixes.

items.what: When a proxy is configured and neither the webrtc_policy param nor CLARK_WEBRTC_POLICY is set, the launcher now auto-adds --force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp and --webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp. Previously opt-in; now the default under a proxy. Tests in tests/test_imports.py pin the precedence order (explicit param > env > proxy-derived default).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: internal/fingerprint/proxy.go + geoip.go resolve --fingerprint-webrtc-ip=auto to the proxy exit IP, which rewrites the ICE candidate the page sees - but nothing stops Chrome from opening a real non-proxied UDP route alongside it. A network-level observer or a STUN-based detector sees the datacenter/host path the HTTP traffic never uses. Add the two switches in ResolveWebRTCArgs whenever a proxy is present; clark's documented tradeoff (breaks real-time media on TCP-only proxies) argues for tying it to the proxy being set rather than making it unconditional.

items.what: The launcher now pins --fingerprint-screen-{width,height} from a 5-entry seed-derived pool mirroring clark_seed.cc, and derives the Playwright viewport as {screen.width, screen.height - taskbar} (windows 48 / macos 95 / linux 0) instead of a hardcoded 1920x947.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already solved this better and earlier: internal/fingerprint/args.go:349-357 pins screen w/h, pins --fingerprint-taskbar-height explicitly rather than trusting the binary default, and sizes the *outer* window (--window-size) to screen-minus-taskbar so inner tracks outer. Clark's version sets the *inner* viewport to screen-minus-taskbar, which makes innerHeight == availHeight == outerHeight - a maximized browser with zero tab/omnibox chrome, a fresh tell. Nothing to adopt; confirms cuttle's design and that the residual 'window does not fill the VNC viewer' gap is inherent to seeds picking 1366x768/1440x900, not a bug clark has fixed.

items.what: Clark's pool is (1920x1080, 1536x864, 2560x1440, 1366x768, 1440x900) with 1920x1080 first and a documented escape hatch: the caller may pass --fingerprint-screen-{width,height} explicitly and the binary uses those values verbatim (clark_seed.cc Screen() checks the switches before falling back to Pick()).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the lever for pain point 1. cuttle's screenChoicesWindows/screenChoicesMacOS pick per seed and the comment at args.go:300 already notes everything must fit inside the 1920x1080 X display. Because the binary honours an explicit pin, cuttle can add a per-seed or per-context 'fill the viewer' mode that forces 1920x1080 (Windows persona) or 1728x1117 (macOS persona) while leaving --fingerprint-taskbar-height and --window-size coherent - no patch change, just a branch in ScreenArgs plus a golden regen. Note cuttle must NOT copy 2560x1440 into its table; it exceeds the framebuffer.

items.what: A deliberately tiny pacing helper: 350ms minimum interval between actions, up to 200ms jitter added only when a wait is already required (never as a free delay), and a separate 900ms cooldown keyed on the same target string so repeated clicks on one selector are throttled harder than distinct clicks. Exposed as pacer.click(page, selector).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: internal/serve/humanize.go is far more advanced per-action (Fitts-law paths, log-normal keystrokes, settle gate, aria-toggle re-click) but is stateless across actions - it has no notion of 'this agent has now clicked the same element four times in two seconds', which is the signature failure loop when a driver retries a swallowed click and cuttle's post-click verify re-clicks on top of it. A same-target cooldown map in humanize.go is cheap and directly attacks that loop. The 'jitter only when already waiting' rule is also a good constraint to borrow: it keeps the p50 latency cost at zero.

items.what: Launch-time linting of caller-supplied args with structured findings (code/level/message/option): flags --enable-automation, --auto-open-devtools-for-tabs / --devtools / devtools=True, --remote-debugging-address outside loopback, --remote-debugging-port without an explicit address, and --remote-allow-origins=*. Policy env selects warn (log), strict (raise), or off.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle passes caller args through to Chrome (internal/serve/pool.go) and already has PinsScreen-style ownership checks in internal/fingerprint/args.go, but nothing catches an agent or driver re-adding --enable-automation or --auto-open-devtools-for-tabs, which silently undoes the whole stealth story with CI green. A small assessArgs() emitting warnings into `cuttle logs` at seed launch, plus a strict mode for the validate harness, is the same idea with cuttle's existing arg-ownership machinery. Adapt the loopback rules: cuttle's daemon binds CDP for the container on purpose, so only the wildcard-origin check transfers as-is.

items.what: New 414-line harness: spins a local TLS server on an ephemeral port with a self-signed cert, launches the patched binary at it, captures the raw ClientHello bytes, parses cipher suites / extensions / curves / point formats with GREASE filtering, computes JA3 (string + md5) and JA4 (t13d..h2_..), and diffs against CLARK_EXPECTED_JA3/JA4 env baselines. Explicitly framed as 'if it matches stock Chrome, patches #40-#44 are a confirmed no-op'. No network access required.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has zero visibility into whether its self-built ungoogled-chromium 148 emits the same ClientHello as stock Chrome 148 - a BoringSSL config drift from the ungoogled base or a GN flag would show up as a JA3 mismatch on every request and no JS-level golden would catch it. packages/browser/validate/ has parity.py and smoke.py but nothing at the transport layer. Porting this (Go, into packages/browser/validate/) gives a cheap tripwire on every engine rebuild, and answers definitively whether cuttle needs a utls-style story at all.

items.what: Stands up a local HTTP proxy, launches through it, then evaluates an in-page RTCPeerConnection that gathers ICE candidates with onicecandidate/onicecandidateerror and an iceGatheringState==complete race against a timeout, returning candidate strings plus parsed {address, relatedAddress, port, protocol, type}. A classifier then fails the run on any private/link-local address or any candidate outside the allowed public-IP set, with a require_raw_candidates() mode for when mDNS obfuscation is disabled.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle spoofs the WebRTC exit IP per seed (ResolveWebRTCArgs in internal/fingerprint/proxy.go, golden-tested in parity_test.go:151) but only at the argument level - nothing asserts the running browser actually stops leaking. packages/browser/validate/smoke.py has no WebRTC probe. This is a ready-made behavioural test for the one stealth vector where an arg-level golden proves the least.

items.what: Documented, reproduced finding: a third-party site/bots/areyouheadless returned 'You are Chrome headless' for the released binary purely because the HTTP request carried no Accept-Language header; adding --accept-lang=en-US,en flipped the same binary to 'You are not Chrome headless'. No JavaScript surface was involved. Also recorded: Incolumitas reported connectionRTT FAIL, and CreepJS still shows its Headless panel with chromium:true.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle emits --accept-lang (acceptLangArg in internal/fingerprint/args.go), so it is covered - but the lesson generalises: a whole class of tells lives in request headers, below every patch and every JS golden. packages/browser/validate/ should assert the outbound header set (Accept-Language, Sec-CH-UA-*, Accept, Sec-Fetch-*) against a stock-Chrome baseline captured once, using the same local-server trick as their TLS harness. The connectionRTT FAIL is also a live hint about patch 0051's network profile values, which cuttle ships.

items.what: Two harness patterns. (a) trusted_local_page(): probes are served from a real local HTTP origin rather than data:/about:blank, so secure-context-gated and origin-gated APIs (permissions.query, storage.estimate, WebRTC) behave as they do on a live page. (b) A font probe table run through document.fonts.check('12px "Family"') for both Windows and Linux family sets, paired with launcher-side validation that refuses a Windows persona unless Arial, Calibri and Segoe UI actually resolve in the configured font dir.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle builds metric-compatible font packs (ops/docker/winfonts/, ops/docker/macfonts/metrics.json) but nothing asserts at runtime that the persona's core families resolve inside the container. A broken image layer would ship a Windows-UA seed enumerating a Linux font set - the single loudest persona contradiction there is, and invisible to internal/fingerprint's golden because it is filesystem state, not args. Add a document.fonts.check() table to packages/browser/validate/smoke.py, and use the local-origin trick there too.

items.what: Full switch surface of the binary cuttle already ships, versus what cuttle emits. Unused by cuttle: --fingerprint-max-touch-points, --fingerprint-storage-quota, --fingerprint-connection-type, --fingerprint-effective-type, --fingerprint-rtt, --fingerprint-downlink, --fingerprint-noise, --fingerprint-location, --fingerprint-audio-sample-rate. Most have seed-derived defaults inside clark_seed.cc so omission is harmless, but two are declared and whitelisted to renderers (patches/0050) with NO consuming patch in either series: kFingerprintLocation and kFingerprintAudioSampleRate are dead switches.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Two concrete items. (1) --fingerprint-noise=false keeps the deterministic seed identity while turning canvas/WebGL/audio noise off - a genuinely useful debug lever for cuttle when a site breaks under canvas noise or when regenerating golden output, and it costs one pass-through flag. (2) Do not reach for --fingerprint-location expecting geolocation to be pinned: it does nothing. cuttle drives timezone and locale from the proxy exit (internal/fingerprint/geoip.go) but leaves the Geolocation API entirely unpinned, so a permission-granted geolocation read reports whatever the host resolves to and contradicts the seed's timezone.

items.what: Neither clark nor cuttle implements geolocation spoofing at the binary level despite the switch existing; clark's PATCHES.md has no geolocation entry at all.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already has the right mechanism for this and is not using it: wsproxy.go pins Emulation.setLocaleOverride per page (methodSetLocaleOverride, wsproxy.go:41) and Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled per page. Emulation.setGeolocationOverride is the same shape of CDP call and would close the timezone-vs-coordinates contradiction without any engine patch. Needs a lat/lon source - internal/fingerprint/geoip.go currently resolves only timezone and locale, so the geo table needs coordinates added.

items.what: Discovery from reading clark's patch layout rather than something they shipped: patches 0002 (window.chrome V8 extension), 0045 (strip HeadlessChrome from UA) and the new 0047 all target headless/lib/renderer/headless_content_renderer_client.cc or headless/lib/browser/headless_content_browser_client.cc - code linked only into the headless shell.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's container runs headed on Xvfb (internal/serve/serve.go:245 appends --headless=false), so all three are inert in production. 0002 and 0045 are harmless no-ops there (headed ungoogled-chromium has window.chrome natively and no HeadlessChrome token), but cuttle is carrying them as if they were load-bearing, and their presence in the series makes it look like those vectors are covered by cuttle's own code. Worth a probe in packages/browser/validate/smoke.py asserting typeof window.chrome === 'object' and no HeadlessChrome token in the headed binary, so the claim is evidence-backed rather than patch-list-backed.

items.what: The project's only agent-facing doc. It delegates the entire interaction surface to vercel-labs/agent-browser (snapshot -i to get stable @refs, click @e1, screenshot for visual confirmation, eval) and adds operational rules of its own: keep one identity stable for a session and never rotate fingerprint/timezone/language/viewport/IP between clicks; restart the driver session after changing executable path, profile, proxy, User-Agent, or fingerprint args; match proxy geography to timezone/locale/network profile; prefer snapshot -i and @ref clicks over raw selectors.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Confirms this repo is not a source for cuttle's pain points 3 and 4 - clark ships no dialog handling, no downloads verb, no screenshot verb, no tab list, no page digest. What is worth lifting is the operational-rule set into internal/cli/SKILL.md: the 'do not rotate identity mid-session' rule and the 'restart the driver session after changing proxy/UA/fingerprint' rule are exactly the mistakes an agent makes against cuttle's per-seed pool, and cuttle's context ls|add plus purge-profile verbs are where that guidance belongs.

items.what: clarkserve is a ~110-line single-process CDP launcher whose docstring positions it explicitly against a multiplexer: 'Lighter than the deployed daemon - no multiplexing. One Chromium process. If you need per-connection fingerprints, spawn one clarkserve per identity on different ports.' Its whole surface is --port, --headless, --data-dir, plus Chromium passthrough. It also binds --remote-debugging-address=0.0.0.0, which its own hygiene.py flags as a warning-level finding.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Nothing to take, and that is the useful signal: the per-seed pool, keep-alive tab, wsproxy session multiplexing and proxy-407 handling in internal/serve/ are cuttle's differentiated surface and have no counterpart upstream. The 0.0.0.0 bind contradicting its own hygiene rule is also a caution against copying hygiene.py's loopback checks verbatim into cuttle, whose daemon binds for the container by design.

items.what: A clean-room provenance document: patch authors are forbidden from reading or statically analysing the commercial binary the patches were inspired by; a separate 'specifier' runs it and writes behavioural notes; every patch header must cite the public source (W3C spec, Chromium upstream, Brave MPL-2.0 file, curl-impersonate MIT) that gave the idea; and a two-question acceptance test gates each patch ('can I cite a public document?' and 'could I have written this without ever seeing the other product?' - both must be yes).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle inherits this patch series verbatim into packages/browser/patches/ and is a public repo with an explicit no-proprietary-binaries rule in CLAUDE.md. docs/THIRD-PARTY.md should carry the upstream clean-room claim and the per-patch lineage requirement forward explicitly, so cuttle's own provenance story does not depend on a document living only in a third-party repo.

items.what: stealth5 flipped the Linux build default from headless_shell to the full `chrome` target (keeping CLARK_BROWSER_TARGET=headless_shell as a rollback lane), added native macOS arm64 and Windows x64 build scripts on AWS, and fixed Windows side-by-side manifest packaging. Validation was three assertions: pytest on test_imports, `bash -n` syntax checks on the build scripts, and a `--version` smoke on the extracted archive.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Already at cuttle's fork point, so nothing to pull - but it confirms the full `chrome` target (not headless_shell) is the supported lane for the binary cuttle runs headed under Xvfb, which is the assumption packages/browser/build/build-linux.sh depends on. The validation triple is also a reasonable floor for cuttle's own release gate in docs/UPGRADE.md: an extracted-archive --version smoke catches packaging breakage that no unit test does.

code_deltas.headline: Between afae698 (2026-07-08) and 548b159 / v0.34.0 (2026-08-10) agent-browser shipped 32 commits across v0.31.2-v0.34.0, and the dominant theme is exactly cuttle's architecture: several agent sessions sharing ONE Chrome over one CDP port. `--pin-tab` (861e76d) gives each session a persisted session-to-target binding with a stable `tab_gone` error, and event-discovered targets can no longer steal another session's active tab. The second theme is "a tab that cannot answer" - a Memory-Saver-discarded renderer versus a renderer paused by a JavaScript dialog are now distinguished by a bounded liveness probe (`ensure_renderer_alive`), recovered with `Target.activateTarget`, and surfaced as `revived` / `activeTabRevived` / `dialogBlocked` instead of hanging the daemon; that plus the pre-existing pending-dialog gate (fail fast with instructions, and stamp a `warning` onto every response while a dialog is open) is a complete answer to cuttle's pain point 4, which cuttle currently has zero code for - `grep -i dialog internal/serve/*.go internal/cli/SKILL.md` returns nothing. Third, the stream server was rebuilt for human-in-the-loop viewing: split reader/writer tasks, latest-frame-wins, per-client `maxFps`, ack pacing with monotonic `seq`, and env-tunable jpeg quality / max frame size - a CDP-screencast alternative to cuttle's fixed 1920x1080 KasmVNC framebuffer. Beyond the delta, their standing verb surface (download-and-wait, upload via setFileInputFiles, screenshot --annotate, an encrypted auth vault with --password-stdin, clipboard paste, batch, diff, read, console/errors, --content-boundaries) is a checklist of affordances cuttle lacks entirely.

items.what: `--pin-tab`: the daemon persists a session-to-CDP-target binding to `{session}.target` (atomic write, 0600, fsynced, survives daemon restarts). Re-attach selects the bound targetId instead of adopting index 0 of `Target.getTargets`. With the flag strict, a closed bound tab fails with a stable `tab_gone` error code plus `data.targetId` and a sanitized `data.lastUrl` for recovery, instead of silently acting on a neighbour session's tab. Sticky per session (`--no-pin-tab` clears it); CDP target ids are accepted anywhere a tab ref is.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle IS the shared-Chrome-over-one-CDP-port case: internal/serve/pool.go gives one Chrome per seed and internal/serve/wsproxy.go fronts it on 9222, so two drivers (or two agent turns) attached to the same seed compete for the same active tab. cuttle has no per-client tab binding at all - a second playwright-cli connectOverCDP picks whatever target is first. This is the single most transferable design in the delta.

items.what: Event-discovered targets never move the active-tab pointer. `Target.targetCreated` (drain) and `Target.attachedToTarget` (auto-attach) both route through one `register_discovered_page` helper that registers without activating; only explicit paths (open, `tab new`, `window new`, `click --new-tab`) activate.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's wsproxy multiplexes CDP for a whole seed. A popup or an ad-opened tab in one driver's page currently becomes 'the' target for anyone re-attaching. The pure-helper split (activate only when the page list was empty or activation is explicit) is ~30 lines and directly portable to internal/serve/pool.go's target bookkeeping.

items.what: `ensure_renderer_alive(session, target, dialog_session) -> Responsive | Revived | DialogBlocked`: probe the renderer with a SHORT timeout; if it does not answer and a dialog is known open on that session, report DialogBlocked (alive, do not touch); otherwise recover with browser-level `Target.activateTarget` (bounded), which reloads a genuinely discarded tab but only focuses a live one, so a probe false positive cannot lose page state. Never rides the 30s renderer-command ceiling.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's daemon has no liveness concept: internal/serve/pool.go and the wsproxy will happily forward a driver's Page.enable to a Chrome Memory-Saver-discarded tab and hang for the full CDP timeout while holding the seed. cuttle's Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled pin keeps background tabs compositing but does NOT prevent tab discard. Add a bounded probe before forwarding renderer-bound commands.

items.what: Recovery is never silent: a tab switch that reactivated a discarded tab adds `"revived": true`, closing onto a discarded successor adds `"activeTabRevived": true`, and a tab paused by a JS dialog adds `"dialogBlocked": true` - in --json, in MCP structured output, AND on the default one-line CLI output. Documented in README, docs site, and both skill surfaces.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the shape of the fix for cuttle pain 4: the agent needs a machine-readable flag saying 'this page is blocked, and by what', not silence. cuttle returns raw CDP through wsproxy.go with no annotation layer, so an agent poking a dialog-blocked page gets timeouts with no explanation.

items.what: Pending-dialog gate in the daemon: `Page.javascriptDialogOpening` is tracked into `state.pending_dialog`; any command that would touch the paused renderer fails FAST with instructions instead of hanging until the client read timeout. Only a dialog on the ACTIVE tab blocks (a background-tab dialog leaves the active renderer responsive), and tab/session management commands are deliberately exempt because switching or closing tabs is exactly how an agent escapes a blocked tab.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has NO dialog handling anywhere (grep -i dialog internal/serve/*.go is empty). A Chrome 'Leave site?' beforeunload stacked over an app modal pauses the renderer; every driver call cuttle forwards then hangs, which is the user's reported pain 4 verbatim. The escape-hatch carve-out (keep tab commands usable) is the non-obvious part.

items.what: While a dialog is pending, EVERY non-dialog response gets a `warning` field auto-injected: "A JavaScript {type} dialog is blocking the page: \"{message}\" - use `dialog accept` or `dialog dismiss` to resolve it". The dialog's own text is included.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Cheapest possible fix for cuttle's blind-agent problem, and it needs no new verb. cuttle's wsproxy already rewrites CDP traffic (humanize.go rewrites Input.*); stamping a warning onto responses, or exposing it on the existing HTTP surface in internal/serve/http.go, is a small change with outsized effect.

items.what: `dialog status | accept [text] | dismiss` verbs, with alert and beforeunload auto-accepted by default so agents never block, confirm/prompt requiring explicit handling, and `--no-auto-dialog` to opt out of the auto-accept. `dialog status` returns `{hasDialog, type, message, defaultPrompt}`. Resolving clears tracked state even if Chrome reports no dialog, so a missed close event can never wedge the daemon into failing every page command forever.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's verb list (up/down/status/open/downloads/logs/purge-profile/context/skill) has nothing here. `cuttle dialog status|accept|dismiss` plus default auto-accept of alert/beforeunload would close pain 4. The stale-state defensive clear is the detail people get wrong.

items.what: `dispatch_mouse_or_dialog`: a mouse dispatch subscribes to CDP events BEFORE sending, and returns early if `Page.javascriptDialogOpening` fires for this click's frame session - because a synchronous confirm/prompt in the handler pauses the main thread so the Input ack can never arrive. Session-scoped so a background-tab dialog does not abort the click.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's humanizer (internal/serve/humanize.go) fires moves without awaiting, but its pre-click settle gate `awaitStable` and the post-click aria-toggle verify both do renderer-bound evaluations. A click that opens a beforeunload/confirm makes both of those hang for their full timeout, adding cuttle's own latency on top of the block.

items.what: `pending_pointer_release`: if a click's mousedown opened the dialog, the button is still logically down; after the dialog resolves the daemon dispatches the deferred mouseUp so the next click is not interpreted as a drag or a double-click.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: internal/serve/humanize.go synthesizes a full down/hold/up sequence per click. If a dialog interrupts between down and up, cuttle leaves the button stuck down with no recovery, and the next humanized click becomes a drag. Small, exactly-shaped bug fix to pre-empt.

items.what: Pre-dispatch hit test: before any click, `elementFromPoint` at the computed click point, descending through same-origin iframes into their coordinate space, tolerant of shadow hosts (`getRootNode().host`) and label/control relationships. If an unrelated element would receive the input, the command errors with `Element '@e3' is covered by <div#consent-banner> at its click point, so the input would land on that element instead. Dismiss or interact with the covering element first (it is often a dialog, banner, or sticky header).` The descriptor is tag + #id or .class, plus " inside <tag#id>" anchoring.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's pre-click settle gate in humanize.go already samples elementFromPoint rects in an isolated world, but only to wait for stability - it does not NAME the blocker or refuse the click. Naming the covering element is what makes an invisible overlay visible to an agent, and cuttle is 90% of the way there already; it is a return-value change, not new machinery.

items.what: Periodic restore-state autosave is skipped while a dialog is pending, because the storage-collection `Runtime.evaluate` would hang against the paused renderer until its CDP timeout. Also skipped inside a 2s quiet period after the last command so a multi-second save never stalls a command burst.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's per-seed auth-state snapshot (cookies + per-origin localStorage over CDP, internal/serve/state.go) does exactly the evaluate that would hang. If cuttle ever adds periodic snapshots, or snapshots on shutdown while a beforeunload dialog is up, it wedges. Two-line guard.

items.what: CDP attach picks the lowest-index LIVE tab instead of blindly enabling domains on pages[0]: `Target.getTargets` order is not activity-sorted, and a discarded tab has a CDP session but no renderer, so Page.enable never answers and connect hangs forever (#1036). Probes index 0 first (fast path for the all-live case), then the rest concurrently; if every tab is discarded, revives the first via the bounded helper; an unrevivable browser fails fast with a clear error.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Direct hit on the known trap. cuttle's immortal keep-alive tab is hidden from drivers, so a driver's connectOverCDP sees a target list cuttle curated - if the surviving first target is a discarded background tab, the driver hangs and the user blames cuttle. Worth reproducing against internal/serve/wsproxy.go's target filtering.

items.what: Persisted tab bindings sanitize the URL before writing: credentials, query string and fragment stripped from http/https, `about:blank` kept exactly, every other scheme (data:, blob:) dropped entirely because their opaque payloads may carry secrets. A corrupt binding file is an error, never treated as 'first-time session', because it may have carried `pinned: true` and silently dropping it removes the isolation boundary.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle persists per-seed profiles and auth-state snapshots and logs URLs. A public repo whose daemon writes raw last-known URLs to disk leaks session tokens in query strings. The fail-loud-on-corrupt rule (never downgrade a safety boundary on a parse error) applies to cuttle's profile store too.

items.what: Stream server rebuilt: each WebSocket connection splits into a reader task and a writer loop so input never queues behind a frame write; latest-frame-wins (only the newest frame is held, read at send time); per-client `{"type":"config","maxFps":N}` (1-120, 0 uncapped); opt-in ack pacing `{"pacing":"ack"}` + `{"type":"ack","seq":N}` keeping exactly one frame in flight; both declarable on the connection URL (`?pacing=ack&maxFps=10`) which is the only way to cover the opening frame; every frame carries a monotonic `seq`.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's human-handoff path is KasmVNC on a fixed 1920x1080 framebuffer (ops/docker/Dockerfile, ops/docker/bin/). A CDP `Page.startScreencast` stream sized to the seed's own window sidesteps the whole framebuffer-vs-window mismatch of pain 1, and the ack/latest-wins design is what makes it usable over a slow link. This is the substantive alternative to fixing VNC sizing.

items.what: Frame encoding made configurable per daemon: `AGENT_BROWSER_STREAM_QUALITY` (default 80), `AGENT_BROWSER_STREAM_MAX_WIDTH`, `AGENT_BROWSER_STREAM_MAX_HEIGHT`, defaulting to the session viewport so a larger viewport is never downscaled unless both are set. Measured: 1280x720 busy page, q80 = 54KB/frame, q20 = 25KB, q20@640x360 = 9KB, frame rate unchanged.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's viewer bandwidth is whatever KasmVNC decides. If cuttle ever exposes a per-seed viewer, per-seed frame size is the natural place to make the window fill the view, and the measured numbers are a free sizing table.

items.what: `set viewport <w> <h> [scale]` applies `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` AND then resizes the real window content area with `Browser.getWindowForTarget` + `Browser.setContentsSize`, with an explicit comment: "Screencast captures the actual content area, not the emulated CSS viewport, so resize the content area to match." Failure of the experimental CDP call is logged, not fatal.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the concrete CDP call pair for pain 1. cuttle sizes `--window-size` once at launch from the seed's spoofed screen table (internal/fingerprint/) and has no per-seed viewer sizing verb; `Browser.setContentsSize` lets a running seed's window be resized to the viewer without relaunching Chrome. Note the fingerprint constraint: outerWidth/outerHeight must stay consistent with the spoofed screen, so cuttle likely wants to size the FRAMEBUFFER to the seed instead - but the mechanism is here either way.

items.what: `metadata.timestamp` on each streamed frame is now real epoch milliseconds (it was always 0 because CDP sends seconds as a float and the code read it as an integer), so a viewer can compute `Date.now() - timestamp` = how stale the pixels it is drawing are.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A human taking over a cuttle seat for a captcha has no way to know whether the VNC frame is current. Frame-age is the cheapest possible trust signal for a human-handoff viewer.

items.what: Default 1h daemon idle timeout: after an hour with no commands (dashboard mouse/keyboard/touch input counts as activity) the daemon saves configured restore state, closes the browser, and exits, because integrations that die uncleanly never call `close` and leaked daemons were observed running for days. `AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=0` restores always-on. The DEFAULT deliberately never closes headed browsers or user-attached ones (a human may be in it); an explicitly configured timeout applies to everything.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's per-seed Chrome pool (internal/serve/pool.go) keeps every spawned seed alive with an immortal keep-alive tab by design; in a container that is a real RAM cost per abandoned seed. The nuance worth copying is the exemption rule: never idle-reap a browser a human might be looking at through the viewer.

items.what: `doctor` no longer hangs on the Chrome version query: Chrome's child processes inherit the stdout handle so a plain `Command::output()` waits for an EOF that never arrives, leaving orphan Chrome processes. Fixed by reading the version from the binary resource table on Windows and bounding the subprocess with a deadline + kill + reap elsewhere.
