items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle shells out to its stealth-Chromium in the container. Any `chrome --version`-style probe in internal/serve or the entrypoint (ops/docker/bin/) has the same inherited-handle hang, and an orphaned Chrome in a container is invisible until the pod OOMs.

items.what: `a11y [url] [--tags wcag2a,...] [--selector css] [--json]`: axe-core embedded in the binary (no CDN fetch), run through a per-frame `Page.createIsolatedWorld` with `grantUniveralAccess`, so page CSP cannot block it, page-owned `window.axe` and AMD loader state are untouched, and cross-origin iframe findings keep their frame selector paths. Partial results are merged without page messaging.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The audit itself is not cuttle's business, but the injection technique is: cuttle injects JS for its settle gate and aria-toggle verify. Doing it in a named isolated world instead of the main world means an anti-bot script cannot see cuttle's helpers as page globals - a stealth win as much as a correctness one. Note this is also the technique cuttle would need for any future 'describe the page' verb.

items.what: Element-not-found errors preserve locator detail: the generic-error flattener was narrowed to the actual locator-miss message family and now APPENDS advice rather than replacing the message, so the role, name, selector or index the underlying error already carried survives. Separately, `find` actions advertised in --help/MCP/docs but never wired into the dispatcher (type, focus, uncheck) were removed, and unsupported actions are rejected BEFORE launching a browser.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Two rules cuttle's error paths should adopt: never replace a specific error with a generic one, and validate the request before doing expensive work (cuttle launches a whole stealth Chrome per seed - rejecting a bad arg after a 4s launch is pure waste). Also a warning about advertising verbs in internal/cli/SKILL.md that the daemon does not implement.

items.what: Invalid CSS selectors return a clean error instead of leaking raw browser evaluation stack traces into text and JSON output.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Same class of fix for internal/serve/http.go and the CLI: a raw CDP error blob costs an agent a turn to parse and often sends it down the wrong debugging path.

items.what: `find role` resolved through `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` instead of a CSS tag-name fallback, so implicit ARIA roles work (<h2>=heading, <ul>=list, top-level <header>=banner), `--name` matches the browser-COMPUTED accessible name case-insensitively as a substring (mirroring Playwright's getByRole), and ARIA presentational-role conflict resolution is implemented (role="button none" is a button; a global aria-* attribute keeps an element's implicit role).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle does not do element location - drivers do. But the regression story is instructive: #1145 fixed this, then #1153 merged from a stale branch and silently reverted it. cuttle's defence against exactly that is the golden.json tripwire; this is evidence the tripwire pattern should extend beyond fingerprint output to any behaviour that can silently regress.

items.what: HAR captures now embed response bodies - text bodies (JSON/HTML/JS) by default, with `--content all` (binary as base64) and `--content none` (headers and sizes only). Shipped alongside a new `derive-client` skill: record a session's traffic once, identify the real endpoints, extract request shapes and auth material, generate a standalone client, and stop driving the browser at all.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The strategic point for a stealth-browser product: the browser is the right tool for the FIRST visit and the wrong tool for the hundredth. A cuttle skill section that teaches 'record once, then call the API directly' reduces the stealth surface the user has to defend, and cuttle already has the ideal capture point in internal/serve/wsproxy.go.

items.what: WebRTC bypass of the domain allowlist blocked at two layers: JS-level `RTCPeerConnection` disable as the primary control, plus `--force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp` appended AFTER user and plugin arguments so a custom policy cannot override the containment (later Chrome switches win). Workers get a bootstrap wrapper that fails CLOSED if page CSP forbids it. Containment is refused outright for CDP/auto-connect/profile/restore/state-replay launches because equivalent guards cannot be installed before page scripts run.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle sets a WebRTC exit IP per seed in internal/fingerprint/. Two portable rules: (1) safety-critical Chrome switches must be appended last, after user `--args`, or they are silently overridable - check cuttle's arg-builder ordering and the golden; (2) refuse a mode you cannot actually enforce rather than pretending. The fail-closed worker wrapper is the right default for any injected guard.

items.what: Chrome honors only the LAST `--enable-features` switch on the command line, so user-supplied `--enable-features=` values are parsed out of the caller's args and MERGED into one preset flag rather than appended as a second switch (which would silently clobber the preset's features). To disable a preset feature the caller must pass `--disable-features=<name>`.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's fingerprint arg-builder composes a large flag set per seed and the output is frozen in internal/fingerprint/testdata/golden.json. If any caller path (context add, extra args, the Helm chart values) can append a second `--enable-features`, it silently drops cuttle's stealth features with the golden still green, because the golden only checks what cuttle emits, not how Chrome resolves it.

items.what: `--webgpu` launch preset: `--enable-unsafe-webgpu` everywhere, plus on Linux `--use-angle=vulkan --use-vulkan=swiftshader --use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader --disable-vulkan-surface` for real pixels in GPU-less containers; automatic private Xvfb for headed sessions on displayless Linux with an explicit warning to NEVER wrap in `xvfb-run` (it kills the display when the CLI exits while the browser lives on) and cookie auth required on the private display; a `doctor --webgpu` probe that renders and screenshots to verify.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle runs headed Chrome on Xvfb in ops/docker. Today a WebGPU-probing fingerprint script sees whatever the container's default is; this is the flag set that makes WebGPU present and consistent, which matters because absent WebGPU on a claimed Apple-Silicon/Windows persona is itself a tell. Also confirms the always-headless `--enable-unsafe-swiftshader` trick Playwright uses for WebGL in GPU-less containers.

items.what: `@agent-browser/eve` extension: a curated ~21-tool agent surface built on the CLI - navigate, snapshot, find, click, fill, press_key, hover, scroll, drag, select_option, set_checked, upload, screenshot, read, get, evaluate, console, network_requests, tabs, wait_for, close - plus a short `instructions.md` that tells the model the workflow (navigate already waits, go straight to snapshot; re-snapshot after actions; prefer read for docs and snapshot for apps; check console and network_requests when a page misbehaves; never expose file paths, refs, or tool names to the user).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the answer to 'what affordances does an agent actually need', decided by a team that ships it. Compare against cuttle's verb list (up/down/status/open/downloads/logs/purge-profile/context/skill): everything page-facing is delegated to third-party drivers, which is the right call, but internal/cli/SKILL.md should carry an equivalently opinionated workflow section instead of only attach instructions.

items.what: Two agent-ergonomics rules encoded in the eve wait tool: (1) a wait that times out returns `{satisfied:false, timedOut:true}` rather than throwing, with the comment "a wait that runs out of time is an answer ('it didn't happen'), not a failure - surfacing it as an error sends models into retry loops"; (2) empty strings are preprocessed to undefined because "models routinely send '' for optional fields they don't mean to use", where a literal `wait ''` would burn the whole timeout.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Both apply to every cuttle verb that can time out or take an optional arg (`cuttle open`, `cuttle downloads [name [dest]]`). The retry-loop failure mode is expensive and invisible in cuttle's logs.

items.what: eve screenshot tool returns the image as an inline data URL for the channel/UI to render, and `toModelOutput` STRIPS both the base64 and the sandbox path from what the model sees, replacing them with "Captured and already displayed to the user." - because surfacing the path invites replies like 'saved it at /workspace/...'. Capped at 4MB inline, path always works as fallback.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has no screenshot verb at all; when it gets one, this is the output contract. The insight generalizes: separate what the human sees from what the model sees, and never hand the model an artifact path it will parrot back.

items.what: eve snapshot tool: retries ONCE after 500ms when the error contains 'CDP error', because a snapshot taken mid-navigation hits transient stale-node-id races; and if the model passes an `@eN` ref where a CSS scope selector is expected, the ref is dropped and a whole-page snapshot is taken instead of failing (the page includes the ref'd element anyway).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Both are 'absorb the model's predictable mistake' patterns. cuttle's equivalents: a driver attaching during a seed relaunch (launch backoff in pool.go) and agents passing a seed name where a context name is expected.

items.what: `download <selector> <dest>`: one verb that clicks the element, subscribes to `Browser.downloadWillBegin` to capture the GUID, waits for `Browser.downloadProgress` state=completed (30s deadline, canceled -> clear error), polls up to 1s for Chrome to finish flushing the GUID-named file, then renames it to the requested path, with fallbacks for when Chrome saved under the original name instead. Browser-domain events are accepted regardless of sessionId; Page-domain ones are session-matched to avoid cross-tab confusion.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has `downloads [name [dest]]` (internal/serve/downloads.go) which LISTS and fetches files already on disk - the agent must click, guess when the file landed, and poll. A click-and-wait-for-completion verb is the difference between one command and a retry loop, and cuttle already pins downloads into the seed profile dir so it has the directory half done. Straight fix for pain 3.

items.what: `Browser.setDownloadBehavior` with `allowAndName` must be re-issued PER browser context - the launch-time call only applies to the default context.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle blocks `Target.createBrowserContext` by default but `--allow-context-creation` opts out. Any driver that creates a context under that flag gets downloads that escape cuttle's per-seed profile pinning entirely. Two-line fix in internal/serve/downloads.go's setup path.

items.what: `upload <selector> <files...>` resolves the element, gets its backendNodeId via DOM.describeNode, and calls `DOM.setFileInputFiles` - it never clicks the upload button, so no native OS file chooser is ever opened.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has no upload/file-chooser support, and this is a pain-4 landmine specific to cuttle's headed-on-Xvfb design: clicking a styled upload button opens a GTK file chooser that is a real X window, invisible to the driver, blocking the page, and only dismissable through the VNC viewer. cuttle should either handle `Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog` in the wsproxy so the native dialog never opens, or at minimum document setFileInputFiles as the only supported upload path in internal/cli/SKILL.md.

items.what: Screenshot surface: `screenshot [path]`, `--full` (full scroll height), `--annotate` (numbered `[N]` labels overlaid on interactive elements with a legend, where N maps to snapshot ref @eN - explicitly designed for multimodal models), `--screenshot-dir`, `--screenshot-format png|jpeg`, `--screenshot-quality`, plus `pdf <path>`. The annotation overlay is injected, captured, then removed. Headless hides native scrollbars by default with `--hide-scrollbars false` to opt out.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has NO screenshot verb - agents must go through the driver or the VNC viewer, which is the friction in pain 3. `--annotate` is the specific idea worth stealing: it joins the visual channel to the interaction channel, so a model looking at a picture can name the thing it wants to click.

items.what: Auth vault: `auth save <name> --url --username --password-stdin` (AES-256-GCM encrypted at ~/.agent-browser/auth, key from AGENT_BROWSER_ENCRYPTION_KEY or a generated key file), `auth login <name>` waits for the form fields then fills and submits, `auth list|show|delete` (show never prints passwords). Credentials can instead come just-in-time from an out-of-process credential-provider plugin over a stdio JSON protocol (`--credential-provider vault --item "My App"`), gated by `--confirm-actions plugin:vault:credential.read`. Explicit rule: never put vault tokens in plugin command args.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has NO secret-injection mechanism of its own, which is pain 2: agents put passwords in argv, where they land in shell history, process listings, and the transcript. A `cuttle auth` vault, or even just a `--password-stdin`-style path into the humanizer's typing, closes it. The plugin protocol is the more interesting half - it lets cuttle stay out of the secret-storage business entirely and shell out to 1Password/vault at fill time.

items.what: `clipboard read|write <text>|copy|paste`: write goes through `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, copy/paste dispatch real Cmd/Ctrl+C/V keystrokes (modifier chosen by target OS at compile time).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A one-command escape hatch for pain 2. cuttle types at ~130ms/char, so a 40-char password is 5 seconds of synthetic keystrokes with a typo roll on every letter; clipboard-write + Ctrl+V is two events, and a human pasting a password is entirely normal behaviour, so it costs nothing in realism.

items.what: Documented typing escape hatches when a custom input component swallows synthesized key events: `keyboard inserttext "..."` (bypasses key events entirely) and `keyboard type "..."` (raw keystrokes, no selector), both listed under a Troubleshooting entry titled "Fill / type doesn't work".
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle does the INVERSE by design: internal/serve/humanize.go rewrites a driver's `Input.insertText` into real keystrokes for runs up to 80 runes (humanize.go:156). So a driver's deliberate insertText escape hatch is silently taken away for short strings - exactly the ones that are passwords, OTP codes, and card numbers - while strings over 80 runes pass straight through. cuttle needs a documented opt-out (env, per-seed flag, or a CDP param sentinel) and internal/cli/SKILL.md should say which path a driver gets.

items.what: agent-browser's own typing is deterministic - `fill` clears and inserts, no synthetic errors are ever introduced into the user's text.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Contrast worth acting on: cuttle injects a QWERTY-adjacent typo plus a backspace correction at 1.5% per printable letter, field-agnostically (internal/serve/humanize.go:62 typoProb, :501, :641). Over a 20-char password that is a ~26% chance of at least one typo/backspace cycle. That is fine in a textarea and dangerous in inputs that intercept backspace or reformat on input - OTP boxes, card-number fields with auto-spacing, masked password fields with strength validation. Suppress typo injection for password/OTP/masked inputs, or whenever the value came from a secret path.

items.what: `--content-boundaries` wraps any page-derived output in nonce-tagged markers carrying the origin: `--- AGENT_BROWSER_PAGE_CONTENT nonce=<n> origin=<url> ---` ... `--- END_... nonce=<n> ---`, and in --json mode adds a `_boundary` object with the same nonce and origin. `--max-output <chars>` truncates. Backed by a shipped `trust-boundaries.md` reference enumerating exactly which outputs are untrusted (snapshot, get text/html, console, errors, network bodies, aria-labels, dialog messages, React tree labels and props).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's SKILL.md has no trust-boundary section, yet cuttle's whole purpose is driving hostile third-party sites where indirect prompt injection is the norm. A nonce is the part people skip and the part that works - a page cannot forge a marker it cannot guess. Cheap to add to internal/cli/SKILL.md and to any page-derived text cuttle ever returns.

items.what: `batch [--bail] '["open"]' '["network","route",...]' '["navigate","http://..."]'` executes multiple commands sequentially in one daemon round trip (args or stdin), continuing on error by default. Documented specifically as the pre-navigation staging pattern: launch with no URL, register routes/cookies/init scripts, then navigate, so interception takes effect on the FIRST real navigation. Batch also propagates the pin/tab_gone recovery object under `result`.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's per-action cost is high by design (~0.5s per humanized click, ~130ms/char typing), so per-command process spawn and CDP attach overhead on top is pure waste. A batch verb, and specifically the 'launch idle, stage state, then navigate' pattern, fits cuttle's `up` + `open` split well.

items.what: `diff snapshot` (current vs last snapshot, with additions/removals/unchanged counts), `diff screenshot --baseline ` (per-pixel with a color-distance threshold, produces a diff image, and reports a structured `dimension_mismatch` rather than a bogus 100%), and `diff url `.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The 'what changed' primitive the brief asks about, already built. For cuttle the screenshot-diff half is the interesting one: it is a cheap way for an agent to tell 'my click did nothing' from 'the page changed but the DOM I queried did not', which is the exact ambiguity behind the swallowed-click problem cuttle's post-click aria-toggle verify tries to solve.

items.what: `read [url]`: with a URL it negotiates `Accept: text/markdown`, retries the same URL with `.md` appended, walks ancestor paths toward `/` looking for the nearest `llms.txt`, and only then falls back to readable text extracted from HTML - no Chrome launch needed. With no URL it reads the rendered active-tab DOM including current auth state and client-side updates. `--outline` gives just headings, `--filter <text>` narrows to matching heading sections, `--llms index|full`, `--raw`, `--json` (reports `source` and `contentType`).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The nearest thing to a 'describe the page' verb, which cuttle lacks. The docs-first negotiation chain is the part worth copying wholesale: for documentation targets it skips the browser entirely, which for cuttle means not burning a stealth seed on a page that would have served markdown.

items.what: `console [--clear]` and `errors [--clear]` expose per-session ring buffers of console messages and page errors; the eve instructions explicitly tell the agent "check console and network_requests when a page does not behave as expected". The streaming docs warn that console travels on an ordered-but-not-durable channel and must be treated as a live feed, not an audit log.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has `logs` for daemon/Chrome logs but nothing that gives an agent the PAGE's console and uncaught errors. When an app error modal is stacked under a beforeunload dialog (the user's exact pain-4 scenario), the console is usually where the real cause is, and cuttle's wsproxy is already positioned to tee Runtime.consoleAPICalled and Runtime.exceptionThrown per seed.

items.what: Tab identity for agents: stable `t1/t2/t3` ids never reused within a session, user-assigned labels (`tab new --label docs`, then `tab docs`, `tab close docs`) interchangeable with ids everywhere, positional integers REJECTED with a teaching error (`tab 2` errors and tells you to use `t2`), and CDP `targetId` reported in `tab list --json` and accepted as a ref because target ids survive daemon restarts while `t<N>` counters do not.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has no tab-list verb at all, so an agent cannot even enumerate what its seed has open, let alone address a specific tab across a wsproxy reconnect. The three-tier identity scheme (per-daemon counter, human label, durable CDP target id) is the right model for a multiplexer, and the teaching error on a plausible-but-wrong input is a pattern cuttle's CLI should copy generally.

items.what: Session-hygiene surface: `session` (current name), `session list`, `session info --json` (lifecycle status, restore failures), `session id --scope worktree --prefix <skill>` to DERIVE a stable session name from the git worktree, and `--namespace` to isolate daemon sockets and state directories. The skill now opens with a mandatory step: `export AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION="$(agent-browser session id --scope worktree --prefix task)"` before the first command, because the default unnamed session is one shared browser that persists across conversations and agents were hijacking each other's pages.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has `context ls|add` and `status` but no session-inspection verb telling an agent which seed it is on, whether that seed is healthy, and whether anyone else is attached. And the doc lesson is direct: cuttle's SKILL.md should make picking a seed a mandatory first step, derived deterministically rather than defaulted, or two agent turns on one machine will share a seed by accident.

items.what: AGENTS.md hard rule: any user-facing flag, command, behavior, or env var must update ALL of - (1) cli/src/output.rs --help, (2) README.md, (3) skill-data/core/SKILL.md and its references/, (4) the Next.js docs site MDX, (5) inline doc comments - in the same change, "Do not skip any of these locations." Plus a CLI/MCP parity rule requiring the MCP server to be updated in the same change, with tests proving the surfaces stay aligned. The thin `skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md` is explicitly a discovery stub that must NOT carry feature content.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle embeds SKILL.md in the binary (internal/cli/SKILL.md), which makes drift between the CLI's real flags and what the skill teaches invisible until an agent tries the wrong command. A CLAUDE.md non-negotiable of the same shape, and ideally a test asserting every CLI verb appears in SKILL.md, is cheap insurance.

items.what: `--action-policy <path>` (JSON with default/allow/deny/confirm lists) and `--confirm-actions <categories>` gate actions behind an approval step, resolved with the `confirm <id>` / `deny <id>` verbs. Categories can be scoped to a plugin capability, e.g. `plugin:vault:credential.read`, so secret resolution is gated separately from ordinary automation.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The human-in-the-loop primitive. cuttle already has a human-handoff channel (the VNC viewer) but no way for the daemon to PAUSE and ask - an agent about to submit a payment form or resolve a secret just does it. Gating on capability rather than on verb is the design detail worth keeping.

items.what: `agent-browser mcp --tools core,network,react` - the MCP tool surface is split into named profiles (core, network, state, debug, tabs, react, mobile, all) with `core` as the default "to keep MCP context small", tool discovery is paginated, and tools carry read-only / open-world annotations so clients can load a large typed surface incrementally. Every tool also takes `extraArgs` for exact CLI parity.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: If cuttle ever exposes MCP instead of a CLI + skill, this is the shape: profiles rather than one flat surface, because the whole point of a small tool list is model context. The `extraArgs` escape hatch is how they avoid re-typing the entire flag surface into schemas.

code_deltas.headline: The git delta since 793cfb3 is tiny - 5 commits, only two functional: a Playwright roll 1.62.0-alpha-<redacted-id> -> 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-05 (40783a0) and two fixes to the installed-skill freshness check (eee5a18, 4f9d85a). The repo itself is a ~200-line wrapper; the real surface lives in the pinned `playwright-core` bundle, so I diffed the two tarballs directly: same 88 CLI verbs, with `upload <files...>` going variadic, `screenshot --type png|jpeg|webp`, `install --global/-g` for skills, and enum hints added to several flag docs. The direction is consolidation, not expansion: three bundled skills now ship inside playwright-core (playwright-cli, playwright-trace, playwright-component-testing), the skill file is treated as generated-from-the-tool (scripts/update.js, .claude/skills/dev/roll.md), and the CLI now nags once a day when the installed SKILL.md drifts from the bundled one. The high-value findings for cuttle are therefore not in the commit range but in the standing architecture - the modal-state gate, the secrets/redaction pipeline, the per-response Page/Modal/Events digest, and the `show` dashboard with annotation handoff - all of which map directly onto cuttle's four known pain points.

items.what: Every tab keeps a `_modalStates` list; JS dialogs and file choosers push onto it, and `defineTabTool` HARD-BLOCKS any tool that does not declare `clearsModalState` with `Error: Tool "X" does not handle the modal state.` The inverse is also blocked: dialog-accept when no dialog is up errors with "can only be used when there is related modal state present".
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the exact fix for cuttle pain #4. cuttle's CDP mux (internal/serve/) passes Input.* and Runtime.* straight through with no a note-taking app that the page is modal-blocked, so agents keep poking the DOM against a stacked beforeunload + app modal. cuttle can subscribe to Page.javascriptDialogOpening/Closed per target in the mux, hold a per-target modal flag, and refuse (with actionable text) any Input.dispatch* / Runtime.evaluate that arrives while it is set.

items.what: Every response carries a `### Modal state` section rendered as `- ["confirm" dialog with message "Leave site?"]: can be handled by dialog-accept or dialog-dismiss`. The `clearedBy` field carries BOTH the MCP tool name and the CLI verb name, and `renderModalStates` picks by `config.skillMode`.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has no response channel at all - agents get raw CDP. But `cuttle status` could carry the same line per seed ("seed abc: \"beforeunload\" dialog open, handle with playwright-cli dialog-accept"), which turns an invisible hang into a one-line instruction. The clearedBy-names-the-verb pattern is what makes it self-healing.

items.what: `Tab._javaScriptBlocked()` returns true when a dialog modal state exists, and `waitForTimeout` then uses a host-side setTimeout instead of `page.evaluate(ms => new Promise(...))`, because JS never runs while a JS dialog is up.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Direct latent bug in internal/serve/humanize.go: the pre-click settle gate samples elementFromPoint rects via an isolated-world evaluate, and the post-click aria-toggle verify re-reads the DOM. With a native dialog open, Runtime.evaluate never returns - so a cuttle click behind a beforeunload dialog does not fail, it HANGS. humanize.go needs the same javaScriptBlocked guard before any evaluate.

items.what: `_raceAgainstModalStates(action)` races every action (and even `page.title()` in headerSnapshot) against a `TabEvents.modalState` emission, so an action that triggers a dialog mid-flight returns the modal state instead of blocking forever.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's humanized click is ~0.5s of curved mouse movement plus a settle gate; if the mousedown fires a beforeunload the whole sequence stalls. The race pattern (act, but resolve early on modal) is the minimal fix and costs one event listener in the mux.

items.what: A `filechooser` page event pushes a `fileChooser` modal state whose clearedBy is the `upload` verb; `browser_file_upload` is the only tool allowed to run while it is pending, and passing no paths CANCELS the chooser.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has NO upload/file-chooser support at all. Worse than missing: an agent that clicks a file input through cuttle gets a native OS chooser rendered inside the Xvfb session, which nothing can dismiss and which blocks the seed until a human opens the VNC viewer. Minimum viable fix in the mux: enable Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog on every target and expose a `cuttle upload <seed> <files...>` verb backed by DOM.setFileInputFiles.

items.what: `upload <file>` became `upload <files...>` (variadic arg, `variadicArg: true` in help.json) in the 1.63 roll.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Small, but it is the only agent-facing signature change in the whole review window - worth mirroring if cuttle ever adds an upload verb, and worth knowing because cuttle's SKILL.md quotes playwright-cli syntax.

items.what: `drop <target> --path=<file> --data="mime/type=value"` synthesizes a real DataTransfer drop from outside the page - the escape hatch for apps with a dropzone and no <input type=file>.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Second half of the upload story. Any cuttle upload design should cover drop-zones too, or agents will be stuck on half the real-world upload UIs.

items.what: Secrets are a name->value map loaded from a dotenv file (`PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SECRETS_FILE`, `config.secrets`). `context.lookupSecret(name)` swaps the NAME the agent typed for the real VALUE at fill/type time; the generated code shows `process.env['NAME']` instead of the value.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the whole answer to cuttle pain #2: the agent never handles the secret, it types the placeholder name. cuttle owns the CDP Input path already (internal/serve/humanize.go rewrites Input.insertText into keystrokes) - that is the perfect interception point to substitute `{{GITHUB_PASSWORD}}` for a value from a mounted secrets file, per seed. cuttle currently has NO secret mechanism of its own.

items.what: `context.redactSecrets(text)` replaces every secret VALUE with `<secret>NAME</secret>` in three places: the serialized response text, every file written by a tool, and every appended line of the console/network log files.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The half people forget. cuttle's `logs` verb and the daemon's own logging would happily echo a password that leaked into a page error or a request body. Redaction must be at the serialization boundary, not the call site - that is the design lesson.

items.what: `locator.fill()` sets the value through the injected script (`injected.fill(node, value)`) and only falls back to `keyboard.insertText` -> CDP `Input.insertText` when the injected path returns "needsinput" (contenteditable, some input types).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Load-bearing stealth finding: for ordinary <input type=text|password>, playwright-cli's `fill` and `type` NEVER touch CDP Input - the value is assigned in JS. cuttle's humanize.go (log-normal keystroke timing, injected typos, insertText->keystrokes rewrite) is therefore bypassed entirely on the most common path, on cuttle's own default driver. Either cuttle's SKILL.md must steer agents to `press`/key-level input for sensitive fields, or cuttle should hook Runtime/injected value-setting too.

items.what: The `browser_type` tool has a `slowly` param that routes to `pressSequentially` (real per-key events), and there is a separate `browser_press_sequentially` tool marked `skillOnly: true` - but the CLI's `type` verb exposes only `--submit`, no `--slowly`.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Compounds the item above: from the playwright-cli command line there is no documented way to force real keystrokes into a text field. cuttle's SKILL.md should document the workaround (`eval`/`run-code` with `page.keyboard.type`, or per-char `press`) for any field where humanized typing actually matters.

items.what: `timeouts.action` defaults to 5000ms (`PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TIMEOUT_ACTION`), `timeouts.navigation` 60000ms, `timeouts.settle` 500ms - all configurable via env, CLI, or config file.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Arithmetic problem nobody has written down: cuttle's humanize costs ~130ms/char and rewrites Input.insertText into real keystrokes up to 80 runes. A 40-char value = 5.2s > the 5s default action timeout, so a `fill` through cuttle can fail with a bare Playwright timeout that reads like a broken selector. cuttle's SKILL.md and `cuttle up` briefing should tell agents to set PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TIMEOUT_ACTION (15000+) when attaching, or humanize should cap total typing latency.

items.what: `browser_fill_form` fills an array of {target, name, type: textbox|checkbox|radio|combobox|slider, value} in one call, each textbox value passed through lookupSecret.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: One round trip per login form instead of six. With cuttle's ~0.5s/click + 130ms/char, batching is worth far more against cuttle than against vanilla Playwright. Note it is NOT exposed as a CLI verb - an affordance the MCP has and the CLI does not.

items.what: Downloads are auto-saved: the `download` page event triggers `outputFile({suggestedFilename, prefix:"download", ext:"bin"})` + `download.saveAs()`, and log entries `download-start` / `download-finish` surface in the very next response's `### Events` section as `- Downloaded file report.pdf to "path/report.pdf"`.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already pins downloads into the seed profile dir and serves GET /downloads + /downloads/{name}, but the agent has to KNOW to poll. Free win: have `cuttle downloads` report status/size/mtime and, better, have the mux emit a one-line notice when a download completes so the agent sees it without polling. Pain #3 is mostly a discoverability problem, not a plumbing one.

items.what: `outputMaxSize` budget: before serializing, list the output dir recursively, and if total bytes exceed the cap, unlink oldest-first, skipping files written by the current response.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's per-seed download dir grows unbounded inside the container. Twenty lines of Go and a flag saves a disk-full incident.

items.what: `screenshot [target]` gained `--type png|jpeg|webp` (inferred from filename extension otherwise) alongside existing `--filename`, `--full-page`, `--hires` (device pixels vs CSS pixels), and element-scoped capture by ref. `scaleImageToFitMessage()` auto-downscales the returned image to fit the model message budget.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has NO screenshot verb. Half of pain #3 is that getting an image out of the container is a hassle. `cuttle screenshot [seed] [--full-page] [--out path]` over Page.captureScreenshot, written into the seed dir and served by the same route as /downloads, is a small, self-contained addition. Copy the hires-vs-css distinction: cuttle's spoofed screens have per-seed DPR, so an unqualified screenshot is ambiguous.

items.what: `### Page` digest emitted on every response: Page URL, Page Title, `Page status: crashed`, `HTTP status: 503 ...` (only when non-2xx), `Console: N errors, M warnings`. `headerSnapshot()` diffs against the last header and reports `changed`, so the section is only emitted when something actually moved.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the page-state digest cuttle lacks entirely. `cuttle status` reports seeds and Chrome liveness, not what the page is doing. Adding URL/title/crashed/console-count per tab (all cheap over CDP: Target.getTargets + Runtime console counters) turns cuttle status into an actual debugging tool. The changed-diffing is the token-discipline trick worth copying.

items.what: `### Open tabs` renders `- 0: (current) [Title](url)` with a `[crashed]` marker, and is emitted automatically whenever there is more than one tab. Plus explicit `tab-list`, `tab-new [url]`, `tab-close [index]`, `tab-select <index>` verbs.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has NO tab-list verb and hides its immortal keep-alive tab from drivers. Agents driving a seed with a popup/OAuth window have no way to ask cuttle what tabs exist. `cuttle tabs [seed]` reading Target.getTargets (minus the keep-alive tab) is trivial and closes a real blind spot.

items.what: `find [text]` / `find --regex "/sign (in|up)/i"` greps the aria snapshot and returns matching nodes with ~3 lines of surrounding context, like `grep -C` - explicitly positioned as the alternative to capturing a whole snapshot.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Pure token economics, and the single most-used affordance in their own SKILL.md examples. cuttle does not own the snapshot, but its SKILL.md should teach `find` before `snapshot` - right now cuttle's skill points agents at drivers without any guidance on which verbs are cheap.

items.what: `snapshot` defaults to writing a YAML file and returning `[Snapshot](.playwright-cli/page-<ts>.yml)` rather than inlining it; `--depth=N` truncates the tree, `--boxes` appends `[box=x,y,width,height]` (viewport-relative CSS px) to each node, `--filename` names the output.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: `--boxes` is the bridge between the aria model and cuttle's coordinate-based humanized mouse: when a ref-based click is swallowed, boxes give the agent real coordinates to feed mousemove/mousedown. Worth naming explicitly in cuttle's SKILL.md as the fallback path, since cuttle's humanize already re-clicks swallowed clicks and agents need to know what to do when that fails.

items.what: Ref resolution failure produces `Ref e15 not found in the current page snapshot. Try capturing new snapshot.` - the error names the recovery action, not just the failure.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Template for every error cuttle emits. cuttle's mux currently returns raw CDP errors (or nothing) when e.g. Target.createBrowserContext is blocked by default - an agent hitting that gets a bare protocol error with no mention of `--allow-context-creation`. Every cuttle refusal should name the flag or verb that fixes it.

items.what: `waitForCompletion(callback)` wraps every action: run it, sleep `timeouts.settle` (default 500ms), then if any navigation request fired wait for load (10s cap), else await the in-flight document/stylesheet/script/xhr/fetch requests - the whole thing raced against modal states.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's humanize.go has a PRE-click settle gate (elementFromPoint rect sampling) but no POST-action settle. Adding a short network-quiet wait after a humanized click would remove a class of "agent snapshots too early, sees the old page" failures, and it is exactly where the modal race belongs.

items.what: `browser_wait_for` takes `time` (capped at 30s), `text` (waitFor visible), or `textGone` (waitFor hidden) - a first-class wait primitive. It is NOT exposed as a CLI verb; the CLI relies on implicit post-action settling instead.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has no wait primitive and no guidance for one. For a stealth farm where pages are slow behind proxies and Cloudflare, `wait --text` beats a polling loop of snapshots (each of which costs tokens and looks like bot behaviour). Worth documenting the run-code equivalent in cuttle's SKILL.md at minimum.

items.what: `resize <w> <h>` is implemented purely as `page.setViewportSize()` - a CDP Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, which does NOT move or resize the real OS window.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Confirms pain #1 is unfixable from the driver side: an agent running `playwright-cli resize 1920 1080` against cuttle gets a viewport override while the actual Chrome window stays at whatever internal/fingerprint sized it to, so the KasmVNC 1920x1080 framebuffer still shows a window filling part of the screen. cuttle must fix this itself - either size the seed window to the framebuffer (Browser.setWindowBounds at launch, or matching --window-size to the Xvfb geometry), or expose `cuttle window <seed> <w>x<h>`. Note the fingerprint constraint: the window is deliberately sized to the seed's SPOOFED screen, so the honest fix is to size the FRAMEBUFFER per seed, not the window.

items.what: `show` spawns a dashboard daemon: a session grid across all workspaces with a live screencast preview, URL and title per session, and a session-detail view with tab bar, back/forward/reload/address bar, and full remote mouse+keyboard take-over (click into the viewport to grab, Escape to release). Flags: `--port` (blocking HTTP server, 0 for random), `--host`, `--kill`.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's KasmVNC viewer is ONE fixed 1920x1080 framebuffer showing whatever seed happens to be there. A per-seed grid with click-to-take-over, plus Escape-to-release semantics, is the better human-handoff UX for a multi-seed farm - and it is what ops/docker/bin (VNC viewer) would need to grow into. The `--kill` and pid-handshake-on-stdout daemon pattern is also directly reusable for `cuttle up`/`down`.

items.what: `show --annotate` (tool `browser_annotate`) opens the dashboard in annotation mode and BLOCKS until the user draws boxes on the live page and types notes; the agent then receives the annotated screenshot, an ARIA snapshot of the marked region, and the notes list. Abort-signal aware, and distinguishes "No annotations were submitted" from a client crash.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's human-handoff story today is "open the VNC and figure it out" - unstructured, and the agent learns nothing from what the human did. code_deltas.repo: clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser (HEAD da07119, 2026-08-16, SDK 0.27.0; open patch series targets Chromium 149.0.7827.114, 150/151 are licensed "Pro" builds behind a run-token gate)
code_deltas.headline: In the last ~30 commits clearcote moved from "a patched Chromium + a Playwright drop-in" to a full agent product: a 20-tool MCP server over one shared stealth browser, a `clearcote-serve` raw-CDP mode that hands the SAME browser to any driver, an in-engine AI agent exposed as a new CDP command `Browser.agentRunTask` (with a record/replay/heal flow cache), an in-engine `Browser.humanizedClick`/`humanizedClickSelector`, and a three-language humanizer with a per-seed motor persona plus an offline detector-emulator that scores it. The stealth work went from "spoof strings" to "prove internal coherence": a self-referential coherence gate with a REQUIRED/KNOWN_GAP contract, launch-time coherence warnings with actionable text, a measured headless window-geometry model (inner<=outer<=avail<=screen), install-integrity manifests, and a documented conclusion that a synthetic seed persona loses to an imported real-machine profile (13/13 fail vs pass on a strict device check). Container work is the closest mirror of cuttle: docker/serve.py launches chrome directly headful on Xvfb and patches exactly the Linux-host-vs-Windows-persona contradictions (Web Bluetooth, Widevine CDM, ANGLE shader dialect). For cuttle the richest veins are the agent-affordance layer (page digest with per-field STATE, modal marking, change-note, element indices), the geometry model (fixes the VNC-fill pain point coherently rather than by force), and the humanizer gaps the motion scorer makes measurable.

items.what: Page serializer annotates every form control with explicit STATE: `[EMPTY; placeholder hint "..."]` vs `[value: "..."]`, `[filled]`/`[empty]` for password, `[checked]`/`[unchecked]`, `[selected: "..."]`/`[no selection]`, plus `opts:[value=text, ...]` for selects and `(disabled)` for dead controls. Line format is `[<index>]<role>label`.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: This is the direct answer to pain point 2 (agents fumbling typing into fields). Agents mistype because they cannot tell a placeholder from a value, or retype into a field that already took the text. cuttle has no page-digest verb at all - the driver returns raw DOM. A `cuttle page` / CDP-side digest producing these annotated lines would remove most typing fumbles without touching the humanizer.

items.what: Modal/overlay detection in the same serializer: any element inside a `role=dialog|alertdialog` subtree is tagged `(modal)`, `has_modal` is set on the page, and a NOTE is prepended - "a modal dialog is open - handle it FIRST. Its elements are marked (modal); items without (modal) are behind it and not usable." The system prompt reinforces it with textual heuristics ("Accept all", "Reject all", "Before you continue").
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Pain point 4 verbatim: agents keep poking the DOM against a blocked page. cuttle's humanizer already has an isolated-world probe (internal/serve/humanize.go awaitStable/probeExpr) - the same probe could walk for dialog/alertdialog ancestors and surface an overlay flag. Note this covers DOM modals only; native Chrome dialogs (beforeunload "Leave site?") still need Page.javascriptDialogOpening, which neither project handles.

items.what: Native JS dialogs are still an unsolved gap in clearcote too - a repo-wide grep finds no Page.javascriptDialogOpening / handleJavaScriptDialog handling anywhere outside the patch series.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Confirms nobody upstream has solved the beforeunload-stacked-over-a-modal case for you. cuttle's serve daemon is the natural place: it already sits on every CDP session, so it can auto-enable Page domain on the keep-alive path, record the last dialog (type/message/defaultPrompt), expose it in `cuttle status`, and offer a `cuttle dialog accept|dismiss` verb. That would be a genuine differentiator, not a copy.

items.what: A per-step "change note" in the observation: `(navigated to <url>)`, or `(the visible elements changed since your last action)`, or - when the serialization is identical - "same URL and elements as the previous step; note that filled input values are not shown here, so a prior type/autofill may have worked even if this looks unchanged". The last wording exists because nagging the model to 'do something different' made it redo working actions.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A cheap 'what changed' primitive. cuttle has no page-state diff; agents burn turns re-clicking. The comment about not nagging is the load-bearing detail - a naive diff makes agents worse.

items.what: `Browser.agentRunTask` takes an optional `planJson` (a flow cache): a JSON array of previously-recorded steps to REPLAY. Each recorded step carries a durable `{role, name, ordinal}` descriptor (deliberately excluding volatile state like `[value: ...]`). MatchDescriptor re-resolves it against the live page; on no match the controller spends exactly one LLM turn to HEAL that slot and then resumes replaying. Every returned step is tagged `recorded|replayed|healed`.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The single best agent-ergonomics idea in the repo. Applied to cuttle it is engine-independent: the daemon could record the driver's successful action sequence per seed+origin and offer a replay-with-heal path, turning a 30-turn LLM login into a deterministic replay that only calls the model where the page actually moved.

items.what: Two new browser-level CDP commands in the open 149 patch series: `Browser.humanizedClick` (bezier move with timing jitter from the LAST KNOWN cursor position, then press+release, all through the standard CDP input path so isTrusted stays true) and `Browser.humanizedClickSelector` (same, but resolves the element centre by CSS selector browser-side and RETURNS the resolved x/y). Both are browser-level so no page debugger attach is needed - navigator.webdriver stays false. Both take `visualize` to draw the trajectory.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle does all of this in Go by rewriting Input.* frames in the wsproxy (internal/serve/humanize.go). Moving it into the engine removes the rewrite race entirely and gets selector->coords resolution for free. Two options: swap to the clearcote engine (CUTTLE_BROWSER_BINARY) and gain the commands, or port patch 130 onto cuttle's own ungoogled tree - it is BSD-3 and targets 149 vs cuttle's 148.

items.what: `show_cursor=True` injects a red cursor dot (fixed-position div, z-index 2147483647, pointer-events:none) that follows real mousemove events, re-injected on load and framenavigated. The agent patch goes further: a 'magic cursor' + one-shot red click ripple rendered INSIDE the page via an isolated world (ISOLATED_WORLD_ID_MAX) rather than a native overlay window, so it positions in exact CSS-viewport pixels, clips to the viewport, and IS captured by Page.captureScreenshot. They removed a cyan target-outline box because 'a real user gets no box around the field they type into'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's whole VNC viewer exists for human handoff, and a human watching cannot see where the agent's cursor is - the X cursor is not composited into the framebuffer the way page-injected pixels are. An isolated-world cursor dot would make the viewer legible and would also show up in any screenshot cuttle later adds. The isolated-world choice matters: it keeps the overlay off the page's own DOM.

items.what: A measured two-regime model of headless window geometry, with the invariant `inner <= outer <= avail <= screen` exposed as `geometry_is_coherent()`. Regime 1 (persona active): the engine spoofs screen AND avail including a taskbar and BEATS a CDP screen override, so the SDK sets no_viewport and resizes the window to the persona's own work area. Regime 2 (no persona): Chromium reports screen == the emulated viewport then synthesizes a frame on top, producing outer > screen - 'not a statistical tell but an impossible state, readable in two property lookups'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Directly reframes pain point 1. cuttle pins --window-size to the seed's spoofed screen and drops --start-maximized (internal/serve/pool.go dropMaximizeIfSized), so the window is coherent but does not fill the 1920x1080 framebuffer. The correct fix is not to stretch the window, it is to make the persona's screen equal the framebuffer for the viewer-facing seed and then fit the window to that persona's avail - satisfying the chain AND filling the viewer. Add geometry_is_coherent as an assertion in packages/browser/validate/smoke.py (which today only checks availWidth==width and a 0..200 height delta).

items.what: `fit_window_to_persona()`: reads [screen.availWidth, availHeight], gets the windowId via Browser.getWindowForTarget, sends Browser.setWindowBounds, then MEASURES the shortfall (on 149 the window reports 33px less than the bounds it was given) and adds it back rather than hardcoding 33 - self-tuning if the engine changes. It reverts if the correction overshoots (outer > avail would trade one impossible geometry for another), guards against an implausible 800x600 work area, and never raises: 'a geometry improvement must not be able to fail a launch'. Explicitly notes --start-maximized and CDP windowState:"maximized" are both no-ops in headless.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's daemon already owns every CDP session, so it can run this fixup itself per seed on the keep-alive tab. The measure-the-shortfall-then-correct pattern and the never-raise contract are both directly portable to internal/serve/pool.go.

items.what: `move_window_to_origin()`: headless leaves the real window at the default (10, 10) while the emulated viewport makes outerWidth span the whole spoofed screen, so screenX + outerWidth exceeds screen.width - the window hangs 10px past the edge on both axes. Only 6% of real single-display captures do that. One CDP call with left/top only (sending width/height would fight the emulated viewport).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A free check for cuttle's headed-on-Xvfb window: assert screenX + outerWidth <= screen.width and screenY + outerHeight <= screen.height in the smoke harness. openbox placement could easily violate it.

items.what: Both window fixups run on about:blank during launch, 'so a page never observes a resize'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's keep-alive tab (internal/serve/keepalive.go) is exactly the right place to do geometry work for the same reason. A resize observed by a live page is a behavioural tell.

items.what: The regime-2 screen table is derived from real captures (the audit_profiles corpus), filtered to self-consistent non-emulated desktop geometry and weighted by DISTINCT /24 so one busy machine cannot skew it, regenerated by scripts/derive-headless-geometry.cjs. Three deliberate deviations are documented: macOS rows dropped (they report color_depth 30, unspoofable), non-1.0 DPR rows dropped (DPR changes what the rasterizer produces), and 3440x1440 capped from weight 12 to 2 ('developers over-represent ultrawides; uncapped it would be picked for ~1 launch in 5').
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's per-seed screen table in internal/fingerprint is hand-authored. The methodology - weight by distinct /24, drop rows whose other surfaces you cannot make coherent, cap developer-skewed rows - is a direct upgrade path and is exactly the kind of change the golden.json tripwire is built to gate.

items.what: A ~20-tool MCP server over ONE shared stealth browser: read_page (text + markdown), get_page_html, page_elements, evaluate_js, wait_for, current_page, get_cookies, list_tabs, navigate, click (selector OR visible text), fill_field (selector/label/placeholder/name), press_key, new_tab, close_tab, screenshot_page, save_page_pdf, save_profile, load_profile, get_egress_info, get_cdp_endpoint.
