The restore-the-previous-URL courtesy is the detail that makes it safe to call mid-task.

items.what: `screenshot_page` and `save_page_pdf`, both writing through `_confine_path`: writes are confined to a sandbox dir (CLEARCOTE_MCP_WRITE_DIR, default a tempdir), basename-only with the extension forced, opt-out via CLEARCOTE_MCP_ALLOW_ANY_PATH=1.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Pain point 3. cuttle has NO screenshot verb - an agent must go through the driver, and the daemon already owns a CDP session that could just call Page.captureScreenshot. Mirror the existing downloads design: write into the seed profile dir and serve over GET /screenshots/{name}, so `cuttle screenshot [name]` is symmetric with `cuttle downloads`. The path-confinement helper is worth copying verbatim.

items.what: SSRF guard on every URL argument: refuses localhost / private / link-local / reserved / multicast / cloud-metadata (including metadata.google.internal and IPv4-mapped IPv6), resolving the hostname and re-checking every returned address, with an explicit CLEARCOTE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_EGRESS=1 opt-out named in the error.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's `open [url]` and its HTTP surface take agent-supplied URLs and run in a container that may sit next to internal services. This is a small, self-contained guard with an escape hatch and it is the kind of thing a public repo is judged on.

items.what: Shared-browser lifecycle: an asyncio lock guards a single instance, `is_healthy()` is checked on every access and a dead browser is torn down and REBUILT transparently, and a lifespan hook PRE-WARMS the browser 'so the agent's first tool call is warm, not a cold launch' (CLEARCOTE_MCP_PREWARM=0 to disable).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's pool already has launch backoff and supervision (internal/serve/pool.go, supervise.go). The prewarm framing is the transferable bit: `cuttle up` could optionally warm the default seed's Chrome so the agent's first attach is not a cold launch.

items.what: `clearcote-agent` CLI: one-shot (`--goal` + `--url`, exits 0/1 on success, `--json` dumps the raw result) or an interactive REPL (`-i`, always headed + persistent) with `:goto <url>`, `:url`, `:model <slug>`, `:steps <n>`, `:help`, `:quit`. Logs go to stderr, results to stdout. The REPL exists so 'you can sign in by hand between goals'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The REPL's reason for existing is cuttle's VNC handoff use-case in CLI form. cuttle has `open [url]` + viewer; an interactive loop where a human signs in between agent goals against the SAME warm session is a natural extension of the existing handoff story. The stderr/stdout split is also the right convention for anything an agent pipes.

items.what: The agent's prompt architecture: request = static system preamble + ONE user message (no growing transcript), with a compact recent-action history capped at kMaxHistoryLines instead of prior page dumps, indices RENUMBERED every step, and a `read` action whose output arrives as `PAGE TEXT` in the NEXT observation. The prompt strongly prefers batching multiple actions per turn ('fill ALL the form fields AND click submit in a single response').
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Context discipline for any agent-facing digest cuttle emits: bounded size, stable step-to-step, no accumulating transcript. Also the specific rules encode hard-won web knowledge (type-with-enter rather than clicking a search button; never click an autocomplete suggestion because it rewrites the query) that belong in cuttle's SKILL.md regardless of whether cuttle ships an agent.

items.what: The motor persona is derived deterministically from the fingerprint seed (mulberry32 + FNV-1a, bit-identical across Python/Node/.NET) into 17 parameters: device_hz 110-155, tremor_hz/amp, OU drift amp/tau, jitter, fitts_a/b, primary_frac 0.84-0.94, overshoot, max_corrections 1-3, approach_bias, plus grab/release, click-hold and key-dwell windows. 'A fingerprint gets one motor identity regardless of language.'
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: internal/serve/humanize.go seeds its RNG from rand.Uint64() per CDP CONNECTION - so the same cuttle seed presents a different motor signature on every attach, and two connections to the same Chrome present two. Deriving the humanizer RNG from the fingerprint seed is a small change with a real coherence payoff, and it also makes humanizer tests reproducible.
items.ref: sdk/python/clearcote/_motion.py make_persona/mulberry32/hash_seed vs cuttle internal/serve/humanize.go newHumanizer

items.what: plan_move decomposes a cursor move into a SUM of minimum-jerk submovements: a primary reaching 84-94% of the distance with gaussian overshoot spread, then 1-2 corrective submovements each closing 55-80% of the remainder, with a 40-120ms motor re-planning gap injected between segments, over an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift plus phase-continuous tremor. Fitts duration clamped 70-1700ms.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's planMouseMove is ONE cubic bezier with a smoothstep ease and a 'occasional overshoot then correction' appended only at the very end. By clearcote's own scorer that yields submovements=0 and a peak-velocity fraction near 0.15 where humans sit at 0.30-0.45. This is the most concrete, measurable stealth critique of cuttle's humanizer in the whole repo.
items.ref: sdk/python/clearcote/_motion.py plan_move/_sample_submove vs cuttle internal/serve/humanize.go:171 planMouseMove

items.what: `_motionscore.py` / `motionscore.ts`: a pure, dependency-free detector-emulator that extracts the feature vector a behavioural collector would compute from a pointer stream - peak_vel_frac (human 0.3-0.45, pure ease-out ~0.15), velocity skewness (human > 0), corrective submovements (human 1-3, a single curve = 0), straightness, dt_mean/dt_std, dt_uniform (i.i.d.-uniform inter-sample timing is a tell), jitter lag-1 autocorrelation (white noise ~0, colored motor noise 0.2-0.8), min-jerk residual, 2/3 power-law fit, and drag grab/release timing. Explicitly framed as a RELATIVE signal for old-vs-new, not an absolute pass/fail, so it can be run offline instead of burning clean IPs.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle has humanize tests (humanize_test.go, humanize_e2e_test.go, humanize_bench_test.go) but nothing that scores realism. A Go port of extract_features over the events planMouseMove/planScroll emit would turn every humanizer change into a measurable diff - the same regression-tripwire role golden.json plays for fingerprint args.

items.what: Wheel handling: anchor the cursor over the content BEFORE the first scroll (a wheel event carries the cursor position, so an unanchored first scroll arrives at (0,0), 'which is not where a hand ever scrolls'), but re-home ONLY when the pointer is nowhere sensible - 'a person does not move the mouse between two scrolls of the same page, so re-anchoring on every wheel call would be its own tell'. The anchor point is upper-middle with gaussian spread, never the exact centre. During a long scroll, a 6% chance per notch of a 1-2px gaussian cursor nudge, because 'a burst of 20 wheel events sharing one identical clientX/clientY is a signature only a script produces'. Ease-OUT envelope (fast flick decaying to inertial settle) with occasional mid-scroll reading pauses.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's emitScroll sends every notch at the SAME driver-supplied (x,y) with no anchoring and no jitter (internal/serve/humanize.go:769). Both tells apply verbatim. cuttle also already tracks h.curX/h.curY, so the anchor gate is a handful of lines.

items.what: 'Pointer presence': one ambient cursor placement (280-620ms of plan_ambient) before the FIRST keystroke of a session that never moved the mouse, because 'a collector reading keydowns with zero preceding pointer events sees input no person can produce, however good the keystroke dynamics are'. Deliberately ambient rather than a move toward the focused field, since gliding onto a control could re-target it and land text in the wrong place.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle humanizes keystroke timing but a driver that focuses via JS and calls keyboard.type produces a keyboard-only session with no pointer history. One ambient burst per page, gated on 'has the cursor ever moved', is cheap. The deliberate choice NOT to move toward the field is the safety detail.

items.what: Measured keyboard finding: with humanize on, keyboard.type held keys 58-107ms while keyboard.press held them 1.4-3.8ms - 'a detector reading the SHORTEST dwell in a session sees the press path, not the type path, so one un-humanised call undid the whole keyboard persona'. Fixed by defaulting press to the persona's dwell while letting an explicit caller `delay` win.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's handleKey does sleep(keyHold()) on keyUp for all key events, so this specific hole is already closed - but the principle (the MINIMUM over a session is what gets scored, so one unhumanized path poisons everything) is the right lens for auditing cuttle's remaining raw-forward paths, e.g. Input.insertText runs longer than 80 runes that bypass the keystroke rewrite (insertTextMaxRunes).

items.what: Humanized fill: focus-click the field, Control+A, Backspace, then type key-by-key with gaussian inter-key cadence (~85+-45ms floored at 25ms), word-boundary pauses, a 6% chance of a 180-450ms thinking pause, and a 2% fat-finger-then-backspace-then-correct on alphanumerics. Values longer than 200 chars bail to native fill because 'humanizing 1000s of chars would crawl'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already does the typo+correction and log-normal timing, and caps the insertText rewrite at 80 runes - clearcote's 200-char threshold and the explicit select-all+backspace-before-typing sequence are worth comparing against cuttle's numbers. The select-all-then-clear detail matters for secrets: a driver's fill() on a pre-populated field otherwise appends or silently no-ops.

items.what: `page.select_option` bypassed humanize entirely and 'dispatched a script-assigned change event, which fails the audit's interaction-select-change-trust check'. Fixed by a shared trusted path (`_select_by_keyboard`) that glides over the <select> but deliberately does NOT click it - 'an open native popup takes the arrow keys for itself, and the trusted route depends on the closed-select stepping behaviour'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A blind spot cuttle structurally CANNOT close: cuttle humanizes by rewriting Input.* CDP frames, but Playwright's selectOption goes out as Runtime.callFunctionOn/DOM commands, which never reach the humanizer. So every dropdown a driver sets through cuttle emits an untrusted change event. At minimum this belongs in SKILL.md as a 'do not use selectOption, click the option instead' rule; at most it is an argument for DOM-level interception.

items.what: Drag/slider findings, measured on a 420px range input: (1) a held button cannot be carried across the engine's own WebMouseEvents, so an engine-routed drag leg reported MouseEvent.buttons==0 on 349 of 354 moves and the thumb ignored them; (2) the engine walks its path asynchronously and answers BEFORE finishing, so it kept moving the cursor after the pre-press pin - a move to (56,120) then down() pressed on HTML at (856,213) instead of the INPUT. Resolution: bare moves stay native, only mouse.click keeps engine routing. Result: press on the INPUT, 97 input events, value 97.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle forwards drag releases verbatim but rewrites the intervening mouseMoved events - it must preserve the `buttons` field on every injected move or sliders (and slider captchas, the exact case a VNC handoff exists for) will silently fail. cuttle's emitMove does take a `buttons` parameter, so verify it is threaded through injected moves under a held button, and add a slider regression test with a measured input-event count.

items.what: Timing sleeps are explicitly OFF-protocol: 'local sleep, NOT page.wait_for_timeout: the latter is a CDP round-trip per call, so it emits protocol traffic that bot-detectors (e.g. reCAPTCHA) can score - a self-inflicted tell inside the humanize path'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's humanizer sleeps in Go inside the proxy, which is already off-protocol - good. But it is a rule worth stating in SKILL.md for the DRIVERS cuttle hosts: a driver that paces itself with page.waitForTimeout is emitting scoreable protocol traffic through cuttle's own multiplexer.

items.what: Ambient motion on page load was made OPT-IN (page._clearcote_auto_ambient, default False) after it 'interleaved with caller-driven input such as a slider drag' and fired on every iframe load mid-challenge, corrupting precise input. `page.ambient_motion(ms)` remains callable explicitly.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: A negative result worth having before cuttle adds ambient motion: automatic entropy bursts corrupt precise gestures and fire at moments no real user produces. Expose it as an explicit primitive, never a per-load default.

items.what: `coherence_warnings()` - a pure, unit-testable launch-time linter emitting {severity, code, message} for incoherent option combinations, printed to stderr by `emit_coherence_warnings` (WARN every launch, NOTE once per process; suppress with quiet=True or CLEARCOTE_NO_WARN). Codes: proxy-no-geo, socks-geoip, platform-host-fonts, gpu-platform, gpu-software, brand-mismatch, version-mismatch, persona-fonts-unreachable, gpu-noise, gpu-noise-string, gpu-string-only, canvas-noise-toblob, headless-render, bridge-no-gpu, automation-arg. Every message names the concrete fix.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's golden.json catches drift in what the arg-builder EMITS; nothing catches an operator asking for an incoherent combination (proxy with no geoip, a GPU string that contradicts the persona OS, extra args that re-add --enable-automation). A `coherenceWarnings(cfg)` pure function in internal/fingerprint, printed by `cuttle up` and testable without a browser, is a near-direct port and fits the existing golden-test culture.

items.what: `persona-fonts-unreachable` warning: the engine reports host INTERSECT claimed-list, so 'a 1,513-font profile on a 115-font host yields ~65 fonts and, until now, said nothing, leaving the caller believing they present an identity they do not'. Fonts are called out as the highest-entropy surface measured (9.45 bits; 35% of machines unique on it).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle ships ops/docker/winfonts and macfonts metric clones for exactly this reason. A count check at startup - claimed persona font families vs families fontconfig can actually resolve in the container - would catch a broken font layer that today fails silently and costs the single highest-entropy surface.

items.what: The stealth-coherence gate: five SELF-REFERENTIAL invariants that need no network, no reference corpus and no second browser - measureText widths must be multiples of 1/512px at dpr=1; measureText must agree between main thread and an OffscreenCanvas worker; getBoundingClientRect must agree with Range.getClientRects; canvas2d+WebGL readback hashes must be identical across two registrable domains in one session; the WebGPU adapter vendor must agree with the WebGL UNMASKED_VENDOR family. Each check is declared REQUIRED or KNOWN_GAP, and the gate FAILS BOTH WAYS: a REQUIRED regression fails, and a KNOWN_GAP that starts PASSING also fails, printing 'promote it into REQUIRED so it can never silently regress'. Modes: --baseline (stock Chrome must pass, validating the gate's own logic) and --selftest (no binary, runs on every PR).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The most transferable engineering idea in the repo. cuttle's golden.json gates arg-building and packages/browser/validate/smoke.py does behavioural spot-checks, but nothing asserts runtime SELF-CONSISTENCY - and a farble/noise patch that hooks the window context but not workers is exactly the bug class this catches. The KNOWN_GAP-that-starts-passing failure mode is the part worth copying literally: it turns every accidental upstream fix into a forced, reviewed promotion.

items.what: Patch 110-runtime-enable neutralizes V8RuntimeAgentImpl::addBindings (early return), suppresses messageAdded reporting, and makes enabled() return false - hiding the classic 'Runtime.enable means CDP is driving me' detection vector while a client is attached.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: No patch in cuttle's series touches v8-runtime-agent-impl.cc (verified: rg for V8RuntimeAgentImpl over packages/browser/patches returns nothing). cuttle is a CDP MULTIPLEXER - every driver it hosts calls Runtime.enable, so this leak is on cuttle's hot path in a way it is not for a one-off launcher. This is a 20-line, BSD-3 patch and arguably the highest stealth-per-line item in the whole comparison.

items.what: Web Bluetooth is compiled in but runtime-disabled on Linux only, so a Linux container serving a desktop persona reports navigator.usb, serial and hid but NOT navigator.bluetooth - 'a combination no real desktop Chrome produces, and an OS-origin tell that survives every string spoof'. Fixed with one launch flag (web_bluetooth_args(), empty off Linux). Measured on their audit: 149/151 -> 150/151, identity coherence 55/57 -> 56/57. The exposed surface is exactly {getAvailability, requestDevice}, matching real stable Chrome.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's image is Linux serving a Windows persona (amd64) or a macOS persona (arm64) - the exact configuration this describes. A grep of cuttle for Bluetooth/WebBluetooth returns nothing, so the tell is almost certainly live. One flag in internal/fingerprint/args.go, gated on Linux, plus a golden regeneration.

items.what: Related precedent in the same family: WebUSB was deliberately KEPT enabled rather than disabled, because disabling only WebUSB left navigator.usb absent while serial/hid/bluetooth stayed present - 'a combination no real Chromium produces'. Measured against stock Chrome on the same host, that split was the single flagged difference in the device-API family.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: The generalizable rule: device APIs ship as a FAMILY and must be enabled or disabled as a family. Any cuttle patch or flag that touches one of usb/serial/hid/bluetooth in isolation creates a tell. Worth an explicit note in packages/browser/patches guidance.

items.what: Privacy Sandbox was UN-disabled by default in 0.23.0: disabling Topics/FLEDGE/Shared Storage/Fenced Frames 'is coherent for a de-Googled persona and incoherent for the default one, which claims to be Google Chrome - and Chrome ships all of them. The audit scored it as an implausible value.' Now opt-in via disable_privacy_sandbox=True.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle builds on ungoogled-chromium, which strips these by default, while presenting a Google Chrome persona. Check whether document.browsingTopics / navigator.runAdAuction / sharedStorage are absent in cuttle's build - if so, that is the same self-contradiction, and unlike a flag it may need a patch to restore.

items.what: Widevine CDM seeded for a Windows persona on a Linux host, because 'a build branded Google Chrome that claims Windows and carries no CDM is readable by any page'. Gated to the Windows persona only (a Linux persona is not flagged for it), fetched host-shaped (a third-party site, since a Linux binary can only load a .so), and cached in the engine VOLUME rather than $HOME so it is fetched once instead of per container. Best-effort - 'DRM must never stop the server coming up'. Measured: audit 97/100 -> 98/100, identity 58/61 -> 59/61.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle already has docs/plans/2607-23-arm64-widevine-spike.md concluding amd64 is tractable and arm64 is not - which maps exactly onto clearcote's gating (amd64 = Windows persona = where it matters). This is the concrete implementation: fetch the x64 .so, seed the profile, cache in the engine volume, never fail the launch. Their arm64/macOS-persona situation is the same dead end cuttle documented.

items.what: Shader dialect: WEBGL_debug_shaders.getTranslatedShaderSource() returns whatever ANGLE's active backend produced, so a Windows persona advertising a Direct3D11 renderer on a Linux host answers with a SPIR-V dump - 'a page reads the renderer string and the dialect beside it and sees two different graphics backends'. The engine (151 r15) can re-translate to HLSL for that query alone; the container enables it automatically when CC_PLATFORM=windows, warns when forced onto a non-D3D persona, and the emitted HLSL is byte-identical to a genuine Windows capture. Rendering is unaffected (same pixel hash both ways).
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle presents an ANGLE/Direct3D11 renderer string from a Linux container (docs/STEALTH-VERIFICATION.md, test/smoke/main.go both assert it), so the identical contradiction is live. Closing it needs an engine patch, which cuttle has the build pipeline for - but note clearcote's fix landed in a LICENSED 151 build, so there is no open patch to copy today. Track it, and consider it a candidate for cuttle's own patch series.

items.what: Font generic binding: Windows binds the `monospace` generic to Consolas (549.81px at 100px), not Courier New (600.11px). A page comparing the generic against the concrete family sees them disagree on a spoofed host and agree on real Windows - 'a check that needs no reference data, only two measureText calls'. Fixed by pointing the generic at the Inconsolata substitute in fonts.conf. A system-ui alias was added but verified NOT to work, because Blink resolves system-ui internally rather than via fontconfig - kept anyway, and filed as engine work.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle ships ops/docker/winfonts metric clones for a Windows persona on Linux and must be making the same generic-family binding decision in its fontconfig. Two measureText calls at 100px is a trivial check to add to test/smoke. The honest 'kept because it is correct and harmless, filed as engine work' handling of the system-ui failure is a good model for cuttle's own known-gap documentation.

items.what: Install-integrity manifests: each SDK snapshots every extracted file's SIZE into .manifest.json at install time and checks the tree before launch (the handful of files Chromium cannot start without on every resolve, the full manifest once per process). Motivation: a missing icudtl.dat CHECK-crashes the browser process during startup before Playwright can attach, so the caller sees only 'Target page, context or browser has been closed' under a wall of engine flags that had nothing to do with it. A tree the SDK installed is wiped and re-downloaded; a caller-supplied tree raises naming the damaged file and the fix. Deleting one file now fails in 2ms with a readable error and no browser process spawned.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle supports CUTTLE_BROWSER_BINARY pointing at an arbitrary engine (that is the clearcote swap path) and bakes its own into the image. A damaged or partially-mounted engine tree produces exactly this unreadable failure through the pool's launch backoff. A pre-launch existence check on the critical files, with an error that names the missing file, is cheap and turns the worst error message in the system into the best one.

items.what: Portable profiles: `--portable-profile` (generate a key and store it beside the profile) and `--profile-encryption-key` (derive at launch, nothing written to disk) keep the cookie encryption key with the profile instead of the OS keystore, so a user_data_dir can be copied between machines. Documented honestly: 'a key stored beside the data it protects means the cookie database is effectively unencrypted at rest'. Verified end to end - a profile copied with its platform-wrapped key removed loses its cookies without the flag and keeps them with either flag; on Linux the control keeps them too because the POSIX key provider derives from a hardcoded constant.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's persistence is a per-seed auth-state snapshot (cookies + per-origin localStorage over CDP) plus a profile store. Whole-profile portability is the stronger primitive - it carries IndexedDB, service-worker state, and site permissions that a cookie+localStorage snapshot silently drops. The Linux note matters directly: cuttle's containers are Linux, so its profiles are ALREADY portable, which means `cuttle profile export/import` as a tarball is nearly free and would beat the CDP snapshot on fidelity.

items.what: launch() moved off incognito to a throwaway PERSISTENT profile dir, because 'incognito cannot load a component-updated CDM, so requestMediaKeySystemAccess(com.widevine.alpha) rejected and the missing EME surface was a tell on a build branded Google Chrome'. The dir is removed on close and again at exit, with a retry - on Windows the browser holds handles for a moment after close, so a single removal leaked a directory per launch.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle blocks Target.createBrowserContext by default (--allow-context-creation opts out) - which, read through this finding, is the RIGHT default for a second reason nobody stated: an incognito-ish context silently loses the CDM and therefore the EME surface. Worth adding to the rationale comment, and worth a smoke assertion that requestMediaKeySystemAccess resolves.

items.what: Documented measurement that a synthetic seed persona is WEAKER than an imported real-machine profile: 'measured against a strict anti-bot device check, a seed persona failed 13/13 while a profile-only persona passed'. Root cause given: with no --fingerprint the farbling machinery never engages, so canvas/WebGL/audio readbacks come back byte-identical to an unmodified browser. profile="auto" therefore selects a REAL captured profile, scored for coherence with THIS host: the GPU term dominates ('a profile claiming an RTX 3080 on an Intel UHD host says NVIDIA in the strings and paints Intel pixels'), screen is asymmetric (claiming a display larger than the host has is the catchable contradiction), browser_major is a hard filter no weight can outvote.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle is entirely synthetic-seed (per-seed screen table, Apple-Silicon persona on arm64, Windows persona on amd64). This is a competitor asserting, with a number, that the whole approach loses on strict device checks. Whether or not cuttle adopts profile import, the noise-vs-no-noise mechanism is worth verifying against cuttle's own build - and the host-coherence scoring rules are a ready-made rubric for auditing cuttle's persona table against the container it actually runs in.

items.what: Profile rotation is per-IDENTITY, not per-launch: 'always serving the best profile makes every customer on similar hardware converge on one identity, and that shared fingerprint becomes its own signal - but re-rolling every launch is worse, since an account whose device changes on every visit is a harder tell'. Default 'rotate' is sticky per key; keyless rotate is stable, not random.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's seed->persona mapping is already stable per seed, so it lands on the right side of this - but the first half of the argument (everyone converging on the best persona is itself a signal) is a real risk for a shared open-source persona table where every cuttle user draws from the same 8-10 screens and GPU strings. Worth thinking about before enlarging the table.

items.what: `verify_profile.py`: launches the binary with a profile and probes the live surfaces (WebGL renderer + full getParameter table, hardware, screen, voices, audio, color-gamut, fonts), printing a PASS/FAIL table of expected-vs-actual per surface and exiting non-zero if anything important diverges. Framed as 'prove it loaded'. Paired with `check_render_coherence()` in the SDK, a page-level probe for a software rasterizer in the unmasked renderer string and for an incoherent vendor/renderer pair.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle's test/smoke and packages/browser/validate/smoke.py check a handful of surfaces; the per-surface expected-vs-actual table is a better shape - an agent or operator can see WHICH part of the persona failed to apply rather than a single pass/fail. `cuttle status --verify` returning that table would make the whole stealth layer debuggable from the CLI.

items.what: SOCKS5 UDP relaying (`socks5_udp` / `socks5Udp` / `Socks5Udp`) carries WebRTC's UDP through a SOCKS5 proxy via UDP ASSOCIATE, and composes with the WebRTC deny default: the association establishes with disable_non_proxied_udp still in force, so enabling UDP does not weaken the leak default. Emitted only for socks5:// because SOCKS4 and http/https have no equivalent. Verified against a live danted's own log: 4 UDP associations with the option on, 0 with it off.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle sets a WebRTC exit IP per seed. This solves the adjacent problem - peer connections that genuinely need UDP fail under the deny default on stock Chromium. If cuttle ever needs real WebRTC media through a proxy, this is the mechanism, and it requires engine support (RFC-1929 SOCKS5 auth and UDP ASSOCIATE) that stock Chromium lacks.

items.what: The engine implements RFC 1929 SOCKS5 username/password auth (stock Chromium does not), so socks5://user:pass@host:port needs no local relay - the SDK strips the userinfo out of --proxy-server (which does not parse it as auth) and forwards --socks5-credentials separately. A companion warning fires because 'geoip cannot resolve a SOCKS proxy's exit IP - timezone/language will NOT auto-match'.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: cuttle strips proxy credentials and answers proxy-407 transparently over CDP, which handles HTTP(S) proxies. Authenticated SOCKS5 has no 407 to intercept, so it presumably falls through - worth confirming, and worth a clear error if unsupported rather than a silent connection failure. The geoip-can't-see-a-SOCKS-exit warning applies to cuttle's geoip layer verbatim.

items.what: docker/serve.py is a direct-exec entrypoint (os.execvpe) that runs chrome HEADFUL on Xvfb by default 'so a real headed browser avoids the headless-mode tells some detectors probe', publishes the loopback-only DevTools port via a socat TCP proxy because 'modern Chrome binds the DevTools endpoint to 127.0.0.1 only and --remote-debugging-address is ignored', and configures the whole persona from CC_* env vars. The README warns bluntly that a CDP endpoint is full browser control and must never be exposed publicly.
items.why_it_matters_to_cuttle: Near-identical architecture to cuttle's ops/docker (headed Chrome on Xvfb/openbox, one CDP port). Two deltas worth noting: they bind chrome to an internal loopback port and socat-publish it, keeping the browser's own listener private - cuttle's wsproxy already sits in that position, so cuttle is structurally safer. The env-var persona surface (CC_PLATFORM/CC_FINGERPRINT/CC_SCREEN/CC_HEADLESS/...) is a compact prior art list for cuttle's own container knobs.

critics:
## Themes nobody swept

**WebDriver BiDi is entirely absent, and it is the standards-track answer to theme 1.** Not one of the eight themes mentions `browsingContext.userPromptOpened`, `browsingContext.handleUserPrompt`, `input.setFiles`, `browsingContext.print`, or `session.subscribe`. A researcher reading the BiDi spec and the ChromeDriver/Firefox implementations would have found that the W3C already specified exactly the design all three projects converged on independently - a persistent event subscription that owns prompt state, plus a single verb that clears it - including the parts the sweep got wrong by omission. BiDi answers the question theme 1 leaves hanging (what happens to a prompt raised while nothing is subscribed) with an explicit `userPromptHandler` capability set at session creation, per prompt type, with `accept`/`dismiss`/`ignore` semantics. That is the policy table gap 9 proposes to invent. BiDi also defines `browsingContext.navigationStarted`/`navigationCommitted` as the navigation barrier theme 6 wants to reconstruct by sniffing CDP frames, and it defines file-input setting without a coordinate or a chooser race. Separately, Playwright ships a BiDi backend (`src/server/bidi/`) that the sweep never opened - meaning a whole alternative transport that cuttle's multiplexer would be blind to (it proxies CDP only) went unexamined. If a driver ever attaches over BiDi, every interception in `wsproxy.go` silently no-ops.

**Prompt injection from page content into the agent is not a theme.** It appears once, as a Snyk finding in the playwright-cli community notes, and is never developed. This is arguably the largest omission given cuttle's positioning: the whole product is logged-in sessions on the user's real accounts, and the agent reads page text as input. A sweep of Anthropic/OpenAI computer-use guidance, browser-use's `SecurityWatchdog`, Browserbase/Stagehand's docs, and the 2025-2026 indirect-injection literature would have produced a concrete surface list - snapshot text, console messages, `document.title`, download filenames, and (crucially) the exact channels cuttle itself is proposing to add: overlay descriptions (`div#consent-banner` is page-controlled text), dialog messages (`alert()` content is attacker-controlled and gap 2 proposes to render it verbatim into `cuttle status`), and `Log.entryAdded` frames synthesized by the proxy. Three of the proposed fixes across themes 1, 3 and 6 pipe page-authored strings into the agent's instruction channel with no framing. That is a theme-level finding nobody surfaced.

**Captchas and challenge interstitials are not a theme, only an aside.** Cuttle's stated reason to exist is Cloudflare and human handoff, yet there is no sweep of how anyone detects "we are on a challenge page", waits for it to clear, or decides to escalate to a human. A researcher would have found Browserbase's `solveCaptcha` behavior and its `captchaImageSelector` config, Hyperbrowser's `solveCaptchas` session flag, browser-use's Cloudflare handling, and camoufox's documented Turnstile posture - plus the recurring practical finding that Turnstile clears on a real click inside a *cross-origin iframe*, which cuttle's root-frame-only isolated world (theme 6 gap 3) structurally cannot probe. That single interaction between two unswept facts is a shipping bug.

**Time and clock control is missing from the waiting theme.** No mention of Playwright's `page.clock` or CDP `Emulation.setVirtualTimePolicy`. A researcher would have found that the standard fix for "the settle gate pays 40ms per press and a spinner never quiesces" is to control the clock, not to sample it faster - and would also have found the stealth counter-argument (a page can detect a virtual clock trivially), which is the honest reason cuttle should not use it. Either way the option should have been priced.

**Cost, density and latency were never measured.** Eight themes propose adding a permanently-attached CDP session per seed, `Page.enable` on every page, per-seed Xvnc processes, screencast fan-out, and post-type verification probes, with effort labels but no memory or CPU numbers. Nobody swept how many browsers fit a node, what `/dev/shm` sizing does, what SwiftShader costs per tab, or what the per-turn latency budget actually is. Playwright-cli's maintainer comment ("still within the rounding error of your LLM completion") is the only datapoint in the entire corpus, and it is used rhetorically rather than as a budget.

**Observability of an agent run is absent.** Playwright's trace viewer - `trace.zip` carrying DOM snapshots, network, console, and a timestamped action log - is the single best existing artifact for "what did the agent actually do and where did it go wrong", and it appears nowhere. Neither does HAR recording, rrweb-style session replay, or Browserbase's session inspector/replay. Every theme independently reinvents a slice of this (a ring buffer of gate outcomes, a `/dialogs` history, a `logs` tail) without anyone checking what the mature answer looks like.

**Frames, OOPIFs and shadow DOM are scattered across themes but never swept as one.** Theme 6 notes the root-frame-only probe; theme 3 notes iframe piercing in ref systems; theme 1 notes agent-browser descends same-origin iframes. Nobody assembled the actual constraint: cross-origin iframes are separate targets with separate sessions under flatten mode, `elementFromPoint` cannot cross them at all, coordinates must be translated per frame, and cuttle's humanizer holds one cursor per *connection* rather than per target. Payment forms, consent CMPs, captcha widgets and embedded logins are all in that category - i.e. exactly the hard cases.

## Repos whose most interesting work got skipped

**browser-use.** Only `browser-harness` was read, and only a daemon file plus one skill doc. The main repo's architecture is a set of *watchdogs* - separate observers for downloads, popups, permissions, security, crashes, DOM stability - which is precisely the shape themes 1, 4 and 5 keep proposing piecemeal. A researcher would also have found its DOM serializer (index-based refs with a cached interactive-element scan), its `include_attributes` token-budget knobs, and its published eval harness (WebVoyager/WebArena/Online-Mind2Web runs). That last item is the only source in the corpus that would answer "does any of this actually raise task success rate", a question no theme asks.

**microsoft/playwright itself.** The sweep read the bundled `tools/backend/` CLI layer and a few server files, and read `injectedScript.ts` only through a minified bundle. Never opened: the tracing subsystem, `page.clock`, `route`/`routeFromHAR`, the BiDi backend, `page.pause()`/Inspector (a human-takeover model), and the whole issue tracker - only *playwright-cli's* tracker was mined. Playwright's own tracker is where the multi-year threads on `connectOverCDP` semantics, download behavior over CDP, and `acceptDownloads` live, and it is where the answer to theme 4's `setDownloadBehavior` question is actually settled.

**clark-browser's lineage.** The patch series was read; its *parent* was not. The `--fingerprint-*` switch family originates in adryfish/fingerprint-chromium (ChromiumFish), and ungoogled-chromium is the base for the client-rects/canvas noise that theme 8 wants to remove. A researcher reading those two would have found the original design rationale for the single-global-seed model theme 8 criticizes, the known list of surfaces those switches cover and miss, and - relevant to theme 7 - ChromiumFish's engine-level input work, which clearcote's own RESEARCH.md rates above CloakBrowser's client-side humanizer. That is the direct prior art for theme 7's hardest question and it was cited secondhand rather than read.

**clearcote.** The SDK and patch headers were read closely, but `docs/RESEARCH.md` synthesizes sixteen projects and none of those sixteen were followed. The canvas-bridge design (forward canvas ops to a real-GPU host) was noted in the community pass and never reconciled with theme 8's WebGL gap, where it is decisive: it is the argument that string-spoofing over SwiftShader is unfixable in principle, which changes gap 4's "pick path A or B" into "path A cannot be completed".

**CloakBrowser-Manager.** The RFB relay and clipboard bridge were mined in detail; the actual per-profile Playwright lifecycle, the license/session-cap logic that produced the best silent-failure post-mortem in the corpus, and PR #50's nginx/KasmVNC 1.5 data plane were only read from prose descriptions.

## Sources never consulted

**The CDP spec itself.** No `browser_protocol.json`/`js_protocol.json` sweep, no experimental/deprecated annotations, no version diff. A researcher would have found several things the themes guess at: `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` carries `pointerType`, `force`, `tangentialPressure`, `tiltX/Y`, `twist` - none of which cuttle's humanizer sets, so every synthesized event has a default pressure profile that no real pointer produces, which is a behavioral tell theme 7 never considers. Also `Input.imeSetComposition` (the correct path for the CJK case flagged in the community notes), `Overlay.setInspectMode`/`Overlay.getHighlightObjectForTest` (a browser-side hit test that needs no page evaluate, directly relevant to theme 6 gap 3), `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia`, `Storage` domain, and `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`'s `worldName` parameter.

**Chromium source beyond `page_handler.cc`.** One file was read, well. Not read: `render_widget_host_impl.cc` and `web_input_event.h` for the actual `kFromDebugger` propagation path (theme 7 gap 6 asserts a two-line fix without reading the consumers), `synthetic_gesture_controller`, `javascript_dialog_manager` in the headed vs headless split, and `content/browser/renderer_host/input/`. Also no bug-tracker pass - the Chromium tracker carries the authoritative history on tab discarding, `background: true` on desktop (theme 3/community notes call it "undocumented"), and file-chooser interception.

**patchright, rebrowser-patches, nodriver.** All three named in the prompt, none swept. patchright is the *implemented* answer to theme 8's `Runtime.enable` gap - it patches out the leak, the `__playwright__binding__` global, the `addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` isolated-world tell, and the console leak, and it documents what breaks when you do (exactly the `exposeFunction`/`page.on('console')` regressions theme 8 gap 2 reasons about from first principles). rebrowser-patches ships the canonical test page with named checks (`runtimeEnableLeak`, `sourceUrlLeak`, `dummyFn`, `exposeFunctionLeak`, `mainWorldExecution`), which is the ready-made adversarial suite theme 8 gap 8 proposes to assemble. nodriver would have shown a CDP-direct design that never enables Runtime at all, and its dialog/file-input handling.

**camoufox.** Named, not swept. It is the strongest counter-argument in the field to cuttle's whole engine strategy (Firefox/Juggler, fingerprint injection below the JS layer, no CDP at all), and - directly relevant to theme 7 - it ships a documented humanized cursor (Bezier plus a WindMouse-style algorithm) with published parameters. That is a second independent motion model to score against clearcote's, which would have turned theme 7's single-source benchmark into a comparison.

**The commercial session platforms.** Browserbase, Steel, Kernel, Hyperbrowser - four products solving cuttle's exact problem, zero consulted. Steel is open source and is the closest structural analogue to cuttle's container half; a researcher would have found its session API, CDP proxy, file upload/download endpoints, and extension loading. Browserbase's live-view iframe with an interactive/takeover toggle is the shipped version of what theme 3 gap 5 and theme 5 gap 6 propose to build, and its Contexts API is the shipped version of theme 5's profile portability. Their docs also settle the upload question (get bytes into the session first, then hand a session-local path) that theme 4 gap 1 rediscovers.

**Detection research as a body of work.** CreepJS's source, FingerprintJS's research posts, Vastel's blog, and the mouse-dynamics literature are all absent as primary sources; theme 7's entire evidence base is one vendor's self-authored scorer, which its own header calls an approximation. A researcher would have found published feature sets for behavioral scoring (velocity profile, pause distribution, curvature, dwell/flight histograms) and, more usefully, the recurring finding that commercial scorers weight *session-level* aggregates - action cadence, revisit patterns, idle structure - over single-gesture kinematics, which would reorder theme 7's priorities away from the trajectory rewrite and toward the inter-action pacing item it rates lowest.

Reviewed against the actual tree (`~/Projects/cuttle`), not just the sweep's own citations. Verified as I went: `packages/browser/patches/0013-window-outer-and-dpr.patch` hard-returns `outerWidth = clark::seed::Screen().width` and `outerHeight = screen.height - taskbar` with no reference to the real frame; `internal/serve/http.go routes()` is exactly the six handlers claimed; `insertTextMaxRunes = 80` and `interKeyBaseMs = 85` / `keyHoldBaseMs = 24` are as quoted; `internal/cli/SKILL.md` has zero dialog mentions; `--fingerprint-webrtc-ip` appears only in `clark_fingerprint_switches.cc` and `internal/fingerprint/proxy.go`, consumed by no patch; there is no `media_values` patch in the series. So the sweep's factual base is sound. The judgment is where it falls apart.

## Already solved, in cuttle or in the driver it ships

**"cuttle's humanizer happily drives a renderer that is frozen behind a dialog"** and **"cuttle is blind to JavaScript dialogs, and its own settle gate is the thing that pays for it"** are filed as agent-blindness. They are not. The sweep's own state-of-the-art section documents that playwright-core keeps a per-tab `ModalState[]`, races every snapshot and action against it, refuses every tool without `clearsModalState`, prints `- ["alert" dialog with message "x"]: can be handled by dialog-accept or dialog-dismiss` into the snapshot, and exposes `playwright-cli dialog-accept` / `dialog-dismiss`. On the default driver the agent is told, in band, on every action. What cuttle uniquely owns is the narrow window the sweep buries at the end of gap 1: a dialog raised while no driver is attached is never replayed on the next `Page.enable`, so the tab wedges permanently. That is real and only the daemon can fix it. It is maybe a fifth of what these gaps claim, and gaps 2, 3 and 8 of theme 1 are largely re-implementing verbs playwright-cli already ships, one layer down.

**"No auto-dismiss policy for the one dialog class that is pure noise"** is worse than redundant, it is self-defeating. Playwright registers a dialog listener on every page, so the daemon and the driver would both call `Page.handleJavaScriptDialog` and the loser gets InvalidParams. The proposed guard is a `bytes.Contains("Page.enable")` prefilter setting `driverHandlesDialogs`. Every driver sends `Page.enable` on every page. The flag is true essentially always, so the auto-dismiss is dead code by construction, and in the rare case it fires it is racing the driver it was designed to defer to.

**"There is no way to capture a seed's page when no driver is attached"** (the `Page.getLayoutMetrics` + `captureBeyondViewport` endpoint) is playwright-cli's `screenshot` verb rebuilt inside the multiplexer. It also cannot see the thing that motivated the whole sweep. Three separate gaps across themes 1 and 3 propose screenshots; only the framebuffer grab is a real capability, and the CDP one should be dropped rather than shipped alongside it.

**"No aggregated view of what exists across seeds"** and **"No session-inspection verb"** overstate the build. `chromePool.status()` already returns pid/port/seed/connections/timezone/locale/proxy on `GET /`, and `runningSeeds` in `internal/cli/commands.go` already fetches it and discards everything but auth state. That is a display fix, not a new endpoint family.

**"No handling for renderer-discarded targets"** concedes in its own risk field that cuttle's per-page `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled` pin makes discards unlikely. The only concrete change it then asks for is folding discard-disabling into `--disable-features`, which the gap itself warns will silently drop `NoReferrers,NoCrossOriginReferrers,MinimalReferrers` if done naively. Net expected value is negative.

## Would break stealth coherence

**"No post-launch geometry verification anywhere"** is the worst recommendation in the sweep, specifically the second half: "add a one-shot fit in `internal/serve/pool.go`: `Browser.getWindowForTarget` -> `Browser.setContentsSize`". Patch 0013 returns `outerWidth`/`outerHeight` as constants derived from the spoofed screen. They do not track the real window. Clearcote's `fitPlan()` converges because in their engine `outer*` is real, so measuring the shortfall and adding it back closes the gap. Ported onto cuttle it re-reads a constant: the measured shortfall never changes no matter how many times you resize, so the loop either no-ops or walks `window.inner*` away from any value the persona explains while `outer*` and `screen.*` sit still. That is the exact incoherence `ScreenArgs` and `dropMaximizeIfSized` exist to prevent, arrived at by the front door.

The same kill lands on **"Nothing stops a driver from destroying the geometry the fingerprint layer just established"**, which says to "make the rewrite-to-setContentsSize variant the default so the common case (a viewer asking the page to fill its canvas) still works". That is a viewer silently setting `inner*` to the size of a human's browser tab. Block `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` and `Browser.setWindowBounds` with a CDP error, mirroring `--allow-context-creation`. Do not rewrite them into a resize that the spoof cannot follow.

**"The X framebuffer is a fixed 1920x1080..."** contradicts its own theme. Gap 1 says run xrandr "on the FIRST attach for a seed"; gap 8 in the same theme says the resize primitive must run "before Chrome launches". Gap 8 is right. A mid-session RandR resize fires real resize and visualViewport events in a live page, and it makes the framebuffer equal to the window, which is exactly the condition under which the entrypoint's `--start-maximized` starts looking harmless again. `dropMaximizeIfSized` is currently the only thing keeping that flag from stretching `inner*` past the spoofed `outer*`.

**"cuttle has NO secret mechanism of its own"**, part (c): redaction applied to the CDP wire. Byte-replacing a secret inside forwarded frames corrupts base64 `Network.getResponseBody`, `Page.captureScreenshot` payloads and `IO.read` chunks, while simultaneously missing the common case where the value appears JSON-escaped rather than literal. Playwright's `redactSecrets` is safe because it runs on rendered text at three known chokepoints, not on a transport. Ship part (b), the `{{cuttle:NAME}}` sentinel expanded in `handleInsertText`. It is genuinely driver-agnostic and strictly better than playwright's post-hoc scrub, because the literal never enters the call log at all. Drop part (c).

**"No clipboard path exists anywhere in cuttle"**, part (c): "give the humanizer a paste path... the ONLY way to fill fields that reject synthesized keystrokes". A field that receives its entire value with zero keydown/keyup is the `fill()` tell in a new costume, the one CloakBrowser's own README says reCAPTCHA behavioral analysis flags, and the one cuttle's insertText rewrite exists to eliminate. The XTEST variant additionally needs window activation, which on the shared `:99` display yanks focus away from every other seed in the container. Keep the clipboard on the human-handoff leg (parts a, b, d) and delete the automation paste path.

**"Humanization is a single container-lifetime boolean"** proposes a live `off` tier, then mitigates the obvious hazard with "refuse to apply `off` to a session that has already emitted humanized input to the same top-level origin". cuttle cannot implement that mitigation. The proxy tracks no navigation state at all; that is the entire premise of theme 6 gap 1. The safety valve depends on a gap the same sweep says is unbuilt. Ship the speed tiers that stay inside human envelopes and leave `off` at daemon-start only.

**"No pre-goal pointer entropy, and the cursor starts at the origin"**, part (b): a daemon goroutine injecting mouse moves the driver never requested, into a page the agent may be mid-gesture on. cuttle already deleted its off-centre press re-aim because a stray micro-move between approach and press broke Material/CDK selects. This is the same failure with a longer fuse. Part (a), seeding `curX`/`curY` off `(0,0)`, is nearly free and should ship on its own.

## Cargo cult

**"Every seed's Chrome shares one X display (:99)... give each seed its own Xvnc display like the manager does"**. CloakBrowser-Manager is a profile manager: a human looks at one profile at a time, N is small, and there is no headless mode because the viewer *is* the product. cuttle's primary deployment has `CUTTLE_VNC` unset. Spawning N Xvnc processes, N openbox instances and N framebuffers to serve a surface most deployments never open is copying the shape of a different product. The cheap tier inside the same gap, `xdotool windowactivate` on the seed being handed off, is the entire real requirement.

**"No 'what changed since my last action' primitive at any level"** talks itself out of existing. agent-browser has `diff_snapshots` because it owns the snapshot; cuttle owns neither snapshot nor screenshot, and the gap concludes "leave the semantic diff to the drivers". What remains is passing `dedup=1` through one query string. That is a line of code inside another gap, not a gap.

**"Single global --fingerprint seed per persona"** is a straight Brave transplant via clearcote. Per-eTLD+1 farbling exists to stop cross-site tracking of one real human across sites they did not choose to link. cuttle's seeds are disposable synthetic identities whose selling point is that they stay identical across sessions so logins persist. "Two unrelated sites can link a cuttle persona to itself" is not a threat cuttle has. The cost is touching every noise consumer plus a build-failure-grade migration. The gap half-concedes this ("partly a deliberate cuttle design choice") and then files it anyway.

**"Three CDP input surfaces bypass the humanizer entirely"** reaches the right answer in its own risk field and then buries it: log one warning when an unhandled `Input.*` crosses a humanize-enabled session, and build nothing until that warning fires. Writing touch, drag and synthesizeScrollGesture handlers for a desktop-persona proxy that has never observed one of those methods is exactly the "no abstraction for a hypothetical caller" the non-negotiables forbid.

**"cuttle has no notion of which attached client owns which tab"**, rated critical / effort large. agent-browser needs `tab_binding.rs` because its daemon multiplexes *sessions* inside one browser. cuttle multiplexes *seeds*, SKILL.md already documents one driver at a time, and the answer to two agents is two seeds, which is the product. The non-strict half (remember the target and re-select it on reconnect) is defensible and small. The strict half, filtering `Target.getTargets` and `/json/list` per client, is a large build against an invented caller that also hands a future bug a lie to hide behind.

## One cross-theme contradiction worth resolving before any of this ships

Theme 2 says to print `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TIMEOUT_ACTION=30000` on the attach line in `internal/cli/drivers.go:59`, calling it "the single highest-leverage line in the repo". Themes 1 and 6 say the top pain is silent hangs on blocked pages and that everything should fail fast. Raising the driver's action timeout sixfold makes every blocked-page failure take 30 seconds to surface, globally, so that long values can be typed. Fix the cap instead: `insertTextMaxRunes = 80` at a measured ~110 to 135ms per char is a 9 to 11 second budget against a verified 5000ms default (`README.md:558`), so the cap is roughly 2x too large and the 38-to-80-rune band times out today. Lower it, and split rather than forward verbatim above it.

## What survives the attack cleanly

The WebRTC no-op (switch declared, zero consumers, and cuttle pays a live proxy round-trip in `ResolveWebRTCArgs` to compute a value nothing reads, while `docs/STEALTH-VERIFICATION.md` claims it works), the missing `MediaValues` patch (no `media_values` file anywhere in the series, and 0013 pins DPR 2.0 for macos, so every arm64 seed reports `devicePixelRatio === 2` with `matchMedia('(resolution: 2dppx)')` false), the AnalyserNode cherry-pick, the SKILL.md "Blocked page" section, the desktop framebuffer grab, and the daemon-side dialog observer scoped strictly to the unattached and re-attach windows. Those six are the sweep.

One caveat on the framebuffer grab: `GET /api/get_screenshot` against the shared `:99` returns every live seed's window in a single image, over the same loopback port that already serves `/downloads`. In a multi-seed container that is a cross-identity leak. Crop to the seed's window via `xdotool getwindowgeometry` on the pool's stored PID. That is the fix, not per-seed Xvnc.
cross_session_notes:
Three patterns are only visible across the batch.

(1) Every real driving session converged on the same escape hatch - raw JS via `run-code` / `--raw eval` - and each time it was a workaround for a missing cuttle capability, not a preference. Session 2 used it to fill 1049 chars (because humanized typing would have blocked for minutes), to read billing text (because snapshots were drowned in console chrome), and to verify a textbox was empty (because there is no 'what is on screen' verb). Session 4, auditing the source read-only, independently proved why that is dangerous: cuttle's humanizer intercepts exactly two CDP methods, `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` and `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` (humanize.go:127-130), so anything going through `Runtime.evaluate` bypasses humanization entirely AND produces isTrusted=false. The friction and the stealth regression are the same defect: cuttle makes the safe path slow and gives agents no fast safe alternative, so they route around the whole architecture. A bulk-text/paste verb and a blessed read-extraction path would close both at once.

(2) Session 4 also documents that cuttle's own SKILL.md is factually stale in two places agents rely on: SKILL.md:199-206 claims typing is 'rewritten into human-paced motion' when `fill`/`type` actually go through `Input.insertText`, which the humanizer never sees (`rg -n \"insertText\" cuttle` -> zero hits), and SKILL.md:200 claims 'off-centre clicks' that humanize.go:398-403 explicitly removed. Session 2's agent used `box.fill(txt)` believing it was the humanized path. Docs drift here directly caused a wrong stealth decision in a live session.

(3) Secrets are structurally unprotected on the path agents actually take. Session 4 established that playwright-cli's `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SECRETS_FILE` substitution reaches only `type` and form-fill, never `run-code` - the vm sandbox has no `process`, so a secret inside run-code must be written literally into the shell command, landing in argv and the transcript before redaction (which only touches output) can run. Session 2's agent had already adopted run-code as its default fill mechanism for non-secret text; the same reflex on a login form would leak the credential. cuttle has no secret-injection verb of its own, so the only protection is a driver feature that the dominant driving style silently disables.

(4) Both audit sessions (3 and 4) exist at all because someone had to reverse-engineer cuttle's behaviour from source to answer questions an agent should be able to ask the daemon - which persona am I, is this input humanized, what is blocking my click. That is itself a diagnostics gap: two full subagent sessions of pure source reading substituted for introspection cuttle does not expose.

Both sessions ran against the SAME cuttle container at the same time on 2026-08-07, and each was the other's invisible saboteur - session 1 saw "two a SaaS console tabs" appear and its filled a note-taking app form vanish; session 2 saw "a note-taking app, a cloud provider, an internal tool tabs" appear and its document focus stolen mid-edit. Neither could see the other, neither could name it from cuttle output, and both independently invented the same class of workaround (foreground the tab, then assert state before/after every write). That is the strongest signal in the batch: cuttle multiplexes CDP but exposes no notion of who else is attached or which targets are claimed, and the failure mode is always silent - clicks land nowhere, selectAll no-ops, forms are closed out from under the agent, and the error surfaced to the agent blames the selector.

Second cross-cutting pattern: in both sessions the agent stopped using playwright-cli's own click/fill verbs within the first few minutes and never went back, because actionability checks never settle on animated SPA/consent UIs. Session 1 fell to raw coordinate mouse events; session 2 fell to DOM .click() dispatch. Both are downgrades for a stealth browser (DOM dispatch produces untrusted events; coordinate clicking requires an extra JS round-trip per click). cuttle's own SKILL.md says nothing about this, so each session paid the discovery cost separately.

Five of the six sessions never touched a browser at all, and the one that did (S44) used cuttle purely as infrastructure - starting the container, curling its CDP /json/version, inspecting its image architecture - never as a page-driving tool. That absence is itself the signal: this batch cannot speak to page-level friction, and any conclusion about selectors, dialogs, or the VNC viewer would have to come from a different sample.

What this batch does show, consistently, is that cuttle's rough edges live at the operate-and-observe boundary, not the drive-a-page boundary. The same root cause appears four times in session 4 in different clothes: there is no machine-readable way to ask a running cuttle anything about itself. Is it ready to accept an attach? Which persona/arch is this seed serving? What address can *this* caller reach the CDP endpoint on? Is the port exposed to anything beyond loopback? Each unanswered question produced a workaround - a `sleep 12` plus curl poll, a hand-maintained manifest-digest pin with a warning comment, a `CUTTLE_SIDECAR_HOST` rewrite branch plus a legacy env fallback, and (only because an unrelated audit went looking) the discovery that an unauthenticated CDP surface was reachable by unauthenticated callers. The second cross-cutting pattern is documentation shape deciding agent behavior. The human's correction - "it feels like you keep falling back to docker compose directly in most occasions" - drew an unusually clear admission: the agent picked the weaker tool because that tool's docs were written in agent-shaped commands (`up -d`, returns immediately, fits a tool-call loop) while the correct one was written for a human watching a dashboard. The cost was concrete: it skipped `cuttle-smoke`, the exact check for the browser path it was regression-testing. Anything cuttle wants agents to do must be documented as a non-interactive command sequence with a readiness gate and an exit code, or agents will route around it.

The a cloud productivity app case burned two full 25-second renders on a page whose text was never in the DOM, and returned a bare `timeout` - the same outcome a slow-but-viable page would produce. One more thing worth noting for the wider audit: in two separate sessions the agent independently reached for glim MCP tools rather than a browser for every research task - and those tasks (reading GitHub repos, fetching articles, scraping HN via Firebase and Algolia) succeeded. Whatever draws agents toward cuttle, it is not general web reading; the demand is for logged-in, stateful, anti-bot surfaces. That should shape which frictions matter most.
